<artifact_plan>
id: gen_plan_experiment_1_idx2
type: experiment
title: Disagreement Direction Test for Sentiment
summary: >-
  Train a simple TF-IDF logistic regression and a character-n-gram random forest on small sentiment data, identify their disagreements,
  and test whether disagreement direction predicts the correct label better than chance and three concrete baselines.
runpod_compute_profile: cpu_light
implementation_pseudocode: >-
  LOAD datasets from Hugging Face: SST-2 and a second small sentiment dataset such as imdb or tweet-eval/sentiment. For each
  dataset, create small-sample configurations by stratified subsampling to sizes {100, 200, 500, 1000} and controlled class-imbalance
  variants. For each (dataset, size, imbalance) and for each random seed in 0..9, fit a simple model pipeline with TF-IDF
  features plus Logistic Regression, and a complex model pipeline with character n-gram features plus RandomForestClassifier.
  Stratify train/test splits so the test set preserves the configured label balance. On the test set, collect every sample
  where the two models disagree. For each disagreement, record both predicted labels, both predicted probabilities, the true
  label, the sample index, and whether the simple model predicted the majority class in that split. Compute the directional-rule
  accuracy on disagreements: treat the simple model as correct when it predicts the majority class, otherwise treat the complex
  model as correct. Compare this against baselines computed on the same disagreement set: random guessing with 50% expected
  accuracy, confidence-based selection by higher predicted probability, and a trust-score-style proxy implemented as nearest-neighbor
  agreement in TF-IDF space without external data. Quantify significance with binomial tests on the directional rule and with
  McNemar's test between the directional rule and each baseline. Save predictions, disagreement records, metrics, and an ablation
  table over size, imbalance, and noise in method_out.json.
fallback_plan: >-
  If the primary datasets are unavailable or too large, switch to sklearn's bundled 20newsgroups with binary subsetting into
  a positive/negative polarity task, or use a small locally created CSV of labeled sentences. If character n-gram models are
  too slow, reduce n-gram range or tree depth and keep the same evaluation protocol. If disagreement samples are too sparse
  at the smallest sizes, pool seeds for that size rather than abandoning the configuration.
testing_plan: >-
  Run a smoke test on one dataset with one seed and size=100 first; check that disagreement samples are produced and that
  method_out.json is valid. Then run one full configuration and inspect the directional-rule accuracy and p-values before
  scaling to all sizes, seeds, and baselines. Validate outputs by asserting that every recorded disagreement has non-empty
  true/predicted/probability fields and that metrics sum to the disagreement count.
</artifact_plan>

cgroups v2 quota\n        parts = Path(\"/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.max\").read_text().split()\n        if parts[0] != \"max\":\n            return math.ceil(int(parts[0]) / int(parts[1]))\n    except (FileNotFoundError, ValueError): pass\n    try:  # cgroups v1 quota\n        q = int(Path(\"/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/cpu.cfs_quota_us\").read_text())\n        p = int(Path(\"/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/cpu.cfs_period_us\").read_text())\n        if q > 0:\n            return math.ceil(q / p)\n    except (FileNotFoundError, ValueError): pass\n    try:  # CPU affinity (cpuset \u2014 used by RunPod, Docker --cpuset-cpus)\n        return len(os.sched_getaffinity(0))\n    except (AttributeError, OSError): pass\n    return os.cpu_count() or 1\n\ndef _container_ram_gb() -> float | None:\n    \"\"\"Read RAM limit from cgroup (containers/pods).\"\"\"\n    for p in [\"/sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max\", \"/sys/fs/cgroup/memory/memory.limit_in_bytes\"]:\n        try:\n            v = Path(p).read_text().strip()\n            if v != \"max\" and int(v) < 1_000_000_000_000:\n                return int(v) / 1e9\n        except (FileNotFoundError, ValueError): pass\n    return None\n\nNUM_CPUS = _detect_cpus()\nHAS_GPU = torch.cuda.is_available()\nVRAM_GB = torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).total_mem / 1e9 if HAS_GPU else 0\nDEVICE = torch.device(\"cuda\" if HAS_GPU else \"cpu\")\nTOTAL_RAM_GB = _container_ram_gb() or psutil.virtual_memory().total / 1e9\nAVAILABLE_RAM_GB = min(psutil.virtual_memory().available / 1e9, TOTAL_RAM_GB)\n```\n\n## Step 4 \u2014 Set Memory Limits\n\nOOM kills the entire container. **Every script MUST set RAM and VRAM limits at startup.**\n\nDecide the budget based on what the script actually needs. Estimate data size \u00d7 2-5x for in-memory overhead, then add ~50% breathing room for temporaries. You may use up to 90% of available RAM/VRAM, but **scale gradually** \u2014 start small (e.g. 30-50%), verify it works, then increase toward the limit. Sequential processing is unacceptable for any non-trivial workload.** A sequential script doing 1000 API calls takes hours and fails halfway. An async version finishes in minutes with proper error handling. ALWAYS ask: \"Can this run in parallel?\" \u2014 the answer is almost always yes.\n\nRead aii-use-hardware skill first \u2192 get `NUM_CPUS`, `HAS_GPU`, `VRAM_GB`, `device`. Set `NUM_WORKERS` proportional to available CPU capacity \u2014 check `psutil.cpu_percent(interval=1)` and scale accordingly (e.g. 30% used \u2192 use ~70% of cores).\n\n## Decision Tree (follow strictly)\n\n- **I/O-bound** (API calls, downloads, web, file reads) \u2192 `asyncio` + `aiohttp` with `Semaphore(NUM_WORKERS * 4)`. NEVER do sequential HTTP requests in a loop.\n- **CPU-bound, vectorizable** \u2192 GPU available: PyTorch on device / No GPU: NumPy vectorized ops. NEVER loop over array elements in Python.\n- **CPU-bound, independent items** \u2192 `ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=NUM_WORKERS)`. NEVER process items one-by-one when they're independent.\n- **Sequential** \u2192 only acceptable when items have data dependencies (each depends on the previous result).\n\n## GPU Rules\n\n- Use up to 90% of available VRAM \u2014 scale gradually (start small, increase after each successful run, keep 10% buffer)\n- Move to device \u2192 compute \u2192 move back: `torch.tensor(data, device=device)` \u2192 `.cpu().numpy()`\n- OOM fallback: catch `torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError` \u2192 `empty_cache()` \u2192 halve batch size \u2192 retry on GPU. Keep reducing until it fits. Stay on GPU.\n- Batch large data: chunk it, `del batch` between iterations to free VRAM\n\n## Parallelism Rules\n\n- **CPU-bound**: `ProcessPoolExecutor` + `as_completed`, pre-allocate result list indexed by submission order\n- **I/O-bound**: `asyncio` + `aiohttp`, `Semaphore(NUM_WORKERS * 4)`, single shared `ClientSession`, `asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True)`\n- Always add `tenacity` retries for transient failures, always set timeouts on HTTP requests\n- **CRITICAL \u2014 `ProcessPoolExecutor` start method**: Default `fork` deadlocks with loguru (and any threading library). ALWAYS pass `mp_context=multiprocessing.get_context(\"spawn\")` when constructing `ProcessPoolExecutor` in any script that uses loguru, threading, or async I/O. Example:\n  ```python\n  import multiprocessing as mp\n  from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor\n  with ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=N, mp_context=mp.get_context(\"spawn\")) as pool:\n      ...\n  ```\n\n---\nThis skill is located at `/ai-inventor/.claude/skills/aii-parallel-computing`. float(complex_accuracy),\n        'num_disagreements': len(disagreements),\n        'disagreement_ratio': len(disagreements) / len(test_texts) if len(test_texts) > 0 else 0,\n        'majority_class': )\n\n    return result\n\n\ndef run_all_experiments() -> list[dict[str, Any]]:\n    \"\"\"Run all experiment configurations.\"\"\"\n    logger.info(\"Starting all experiments\")\n\n    # Load \"__main__\":\n    main()\n", "new_content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Disagreement Direction Test for Sentiment Classification.\n\nCompares TF-IDF Logistic Regression vs character n-gram RandomForest\non small sentiment datasets, analyzing whether disagreement direction\npredicts the correct label better than chance and concrete baselines.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport gc\nimport json\nimport math\nimport multiprocessing as mp\nimport os\nimport resource\nimport sys\nimport time\nfrom collections import Counter\nfrom concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor, as_completed\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Any\n\nimport numpy as np\nfrom datasets import load_dataset\nfrom loguru import logger\nfrom scipy.stats import binom_test\nfrom sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier\nfrom sklearn.feature_extraction.text import CountVectorizer, TfidfVectorizer\nfrom sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression\nfrom sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score\nfrom sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split\nfrom sklearn.neighbors import NearestNeighbors\nfrom sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline\n\n# ============================================================================\n# CONFIGURATION AND CONSTANTS\n# ============================================================================\n\nWORKSPACE = Path(\n    \"/ai-inventor/aii_data/runs/run_q27XJGeAT3TE/3_invention_loop/iter_1/gen_art/gen_art_experiment_1\"\n)\nLOG_DIR = WORKSPACE / \"logs\"\nOUTPUT_DIR = WORKSPACE / \"results\"\nLOG_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)\nOUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)\n\nDATASETS = [\"sst2\", \"imdb\"]\nSAMPLE_SIZES = [100, 200, 500, 1000]\nIMBALANCE_RATIOS = [0.5, 0.7, 0.9]  # majority:minority ratio\nSEEDS = list(range(10))\nNUM_WORKERS = 2  # Container has 2 CPUs\n\n# Memory limits based on container resources (14GB RAM)\nRAM_BUDGET = 12 * 1024**3  # 12GB\n\n# ============================================================================\n# LOGGING SETUP\n# ============================================================================\n\nlogger.remove()\nlogger.add(\n    sys.stdout,\n    level=\"INFO\",\n    format=\"{time:HH:mm:ss}|{level:<7}|{message}\",\n)\nlogger.add(\n    LOG_DIR / \"run.log\",\n    rotation=\"30 MB\",\n    level=\"DEBUG\",\n)\n\n# ============================================================================\n# HARDWARE DETECTION\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef _detect_cpus() -> int:\n    \"\"\"Detect actual CPU allocation (containers/pods/bare metal).\"\"\"\n    try:  # cgroups v2 quota\n        parts = Path(\"/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.max\").read_text().split()\n        if parts[0] != \"max\":\n            return max(1, math.ceil(int(parts[0]) / int(parts[1])))\n    except (FileNotFoundError, ValueError):\n        pass\n    try:  # cgroups v1 quota\n        q = int(Path(\"/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/cpu.cfs_quota_us\").read_text())\n        p = int(Path(\"/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/cpu.cfs_period_us\").read_text())\n        if q > 0:\n            return max(1, math.ceil(q / p))\n    except (FileNotFoundError, ValueError):\n        pass\n    try:  # CPU affinity (cpuset \u2014 used by RunPod, Docker --cpuset-cpus)\n        return len(os.sched_getaffinity(0))\n    except (AttributeError, OSError):\n        pass\n    return os.cpu_count() or 1\n\nNUM_CPUS = _detect_cpus()\nlogger.info(f\"Detected {NUM_CPUS} CPUs\")\n\n# Set memory limits\nresource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_AS, (RAM_BUDGET * 3, RAM_BUDGET * 3))\n\n# ============================================================================\n# MODEL DEFINITIONS\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef get_simple_model():\n    \"\"\"Simple model: TF-IDF + Logistic Regression.\"\"\"\n    return Pipeline([\n        ('tfidf', TfidfVectorizer(max_features=10000, ngram_range=(1, 2))),\n        ('clf', LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000, random_state=42, n_jobs=1))\n    ])\n\n\ndef get_complex_model():\n    \"\"\"Complex model: character n-grams + RandomForest.\"\"\"\n    return Pipeline([\n        ('char_ngram', CountVectorizer(\n            analyzer='char',\n            ngram_range=(3, 5),\n            max_features=20000\n        )),\n        ('clf', RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=100, random_state=42, n_jobs=1))\n    ])\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# DATA LOADING AND PREPARATION\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef load_sst2():\n    \"\"\"Load SST-2 dataset.\"\"\"\n    logger.info(\"Loading SST-2 dataset\")\n    ds = load_dataset(\"stanfordnlp/sst2\", split=\"train\")\n    texts = ds[\"sentence\"]\n    labels = ds[\"label\"]\n    del ds\n    gc.collect()\n    return texts, labels\n\n\ndef load_imdb():\n    \"\"\"Load IMDB dataset.\"\"\"\n    logger.info(\"Loading IMDB dataset\")\n    ds = load_dataset(\"stanfordnlp/imdb\", split=\"train\")\n    texts = ds[\"text\"]\n    labels = ds[\"label\"]\n    del ds\n    gc.collect()\n    return texts, labels\n\n\ndef stratified_imbalanced_subsample(\n    texts: list[str],\n    labels: list[int],\n    target_size: int,\n    imbalance_ratio: float,\n    random_state: int\n) -> tuple[list[str], list[int]]:\n    \"\"\"Create a stratified subsample with controlled class imbalance.\n\n    Args:\n        texts: List of text samples\n        labels: List of labels\n        target_size: Total target sample size\n        imbalance_ratio: Ratio of majority to minority class (0.5 = balanced)\n        random_state: Random seed\n\n    Returns:\n        Subsampled texts and labels\n    \"\"\"\n    rng = np.random.RandomState(random_state)\n\n    # Separate by class\n    class_0_idx = [i for i, l in enumerate(labels) if l == 0]\n    class_1_idx = [i for i, l in enumerate(labels) if l == 1]\n\n    # Calculate sizes based on imbalance ratio\n    # imbalance_ratio = majority_size / minority_size\n    # total = majority_size + minority_size\n    minority_size = int(target_size / (1 + imbalance_ratio))\n    majority_size = target_size - minority_size\n\n    # Sample from each class\n    sampled_0 = rng.choice(class_0_idx, size=min(majority_size, len(class_0_idx)), replace=False)\n    sampled_1 = rng.choice(class_1_idx, size=min(minority_size, len(class_1_idx)), replace=False)\n\n    # Combine and shuffle\n    indices = np.concatenate([sampled_0, sampled_1])\n    rng.shuffle(indices)\n\n    return [texts[i] for i in indices], [labels[i] for i in indices]\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# BASELINE METHODS\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef confidence_baseline(disagreements: list[dict]) -> list[int]:\n    \"\"\"Baseline: predict whichever model has higher confidence.\"\"\"\n    predictions = []\n    for d in disagreements:\n        if d['prob_simple'] > d['prob_complex']:\n            predictions.append(d['pred_simple'])\n        else:\n            predictions.append(d['pred_complex'])\n    return predictions\n\n\ndef trust_score_baseline(disagreements: list[dict], train_texts: list[str], train_labels: list[int]) -> list[int]:\n    \"\"\"Baseline: trust-score style proxy using nearest-neighbor agreement.\"\"\"\n    # Build TF-IDF representation of training data\n    vectorizer = TfidfVectorizer(max_features=10000, ngram_range=(1, 2))\n    try:\n        train_tfidf = vectorizer.fit_transform(train_texts)\n        nn = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=5, metric='cosine')\n        nn.fit(train_tfidf)\n\n        predictions = []\n        for d in disagreements:\n            # Transform test text\n            test_vec = vectorizer.transform([d['text']])\n            distances, indices = nn.kneighbors(test_vec)\n            neighbor_labels = [train_labels[i] for i in indices[0]]\n            majority_label = Counter(neighbor_labels).most_common(1)[0][0]\n            predictions.append(majority_label)\n    except Exception as e:\n        logger.warning(f\"Trust score baseline failed: {e}\")\n        # Fallback to random\n        predictions = [np.random.choice([0, 1]) for _ in disagreements]\n\n    return predictions\n\n\ndef random_baseline(n: int) -> list[int]:\n    \"\"\"Random baseline.\"\"\"\n    return np.random.RandomState(42).randint(0, 2, size=n).tolist()\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# STATISTICAL TESTS\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef binomial_test_on_directional_rule(disagreements: list[dict], majority_class: int) -> tuple[float, float]:\n    \"\"\"Test if directional rule accuracy > 50% using binomial test.\"\"\"\n    correct = sum(\n        1 for d in disagreements\n        if (d['pred_simple'] == majority_class and d['pred_simple'] == d['true_label']) or\n           (d['pred_simple'] != majority_class and d['pred_complex'] == d['true_label'])\n    )\n    n = len(disagreements)\n    if n == 0:\n        return 0.0, 1.0\n    p_value = binom_test(correct, n, 0.5, alternative='greater')\n    accuracy = correct / n\n    return accuracy, p_value\n\n\ndef mcnemar_test(y_true: list[int], pred1: list[int], pred2: list[int]) -> tuple[float, float]:\n    \"\"\"McNemar's test between two prediction sets.\"\"\"\n    # Contingency table\n    a = sum(1 for yt, p1, p2 in zip(y_true, pred1, pred2)\n            if p1 == yt and p2 != yt)  # pred1 correct, pred2 wrong\n    b = sum(1 for yt, p1, p2 in zip(y_true, pred1, pred2)\n            if p1 != yt and p2 == yt)  # pred1 wrong, pred2 correct\n    c = sum(1 for yt, p1, p2 in zip(y_true, pred1, pred2)\n            if p1 != yt and p2 != yt)  # both wrong\n    d = sum(1 for yt, p1, p2 in zip(y_true, pred1, pred2)\n            if p1 == yt and p2 == yt)  # both correct\n\n    # McNemar's test on discordant pairs\n    if a + b == 0:\n        return 0.0, 1.0\n\n    # Use binomial approximation for McNemar's test\n    # For larger samples, chi-square with continuity correction\n    if a + b < 25:\n        p_value = binom_test(a, a + b, 0.5, alternative='two-sided')\n    else:\n        chi2 = (abs(a - b) - 1) ** 2 / (a + b)\n        p_value = stats.chi2.sf(chi2, 1)\n\n    accuracy1 = (a + d) / len(y_true) if len(y_true) > 0 else 0\n    accuracy2 = (b + d) / len(y_true) if len(y_true) > 0 else 0\n\n    return accuracy1, p_value\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# EXPERIMENT EXECUTION\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef run_single_experiment(\n    dataset_name: str,\n    texts: list[str],\n    labels: list[int],\n    sample_size: int,\n    imbalance_ratio: float,\n    seed: int\n) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"Run a single experiment configuration.\"\"\"\n    logger.info(\n        f\"Running: dataset={dataset_name}, size={sample_size}, \"\n        f\"imbalance={imbalance_ratio}, seed={seed}\"\n    )\n\n    # Subsample\n    sub_texts, sub_labels = stratified_imbalanced_subsample(\n        texts, labels, sample_size, imbalance_ratio, seed\n    )\n\n    # Determine majority class\n    majority_class = Counter(sub_labels).most_common(1)[0][0]\n    logger.debug(f\"Majority class: {majority_class}, distribution: {Counter(sub_labels)}\")\n\n    # Train/test split (80/20), stratified\n    train_texts, test_texts, train_labels, test_labels = train_test_split(\n        sub_texts, sub_labels, test_size=0.2, random_state=seed, stratify=sub_labels\n    )\n\n    # Fit simple model\n    simple_model = get_simple_model()\n    simple_model.fit(train_texts, train_labels)\n    simple_preds = simple_model.predict(test_texts)\n    simple_probs = simple_model.predict_proba(test_texts)\n\n    # Fit complex model\n    complex_model = get_complex_model()\n    complex_model.fit(train_texts, train_labels)\n    complex_preds = complex_model.predict(test_texts)\n    complex_probs = complex_model.predict_proba(test_texts)\n\n    # Find disagreements\n    disagreements = []\n    for i, (text, true_label) in enumerate(zip(test_texts, test_labels)):\n        if simple_preds[i] != complex_preds[i]:\n            disagreements.append({\n                'text': text,\n                'true_label': int(true_label),\n                'pred_simple': int(simple_preds[i]),\n                'pred_complex': int(complex_preds[i]),\n                'prob_simple': float(max(simple_probs[i])),\n                'prob_complex': float(max(complex_probs[i])),\n                'sample_index': i\n            })\n\n    logger.debug(f\"Found {len(disagreements)} disagreements out of {len(test_texts)} test samples\")\n\n    # Compute baselines on disagreement set\n    if len(disagreements) > 0:\n        # Random baseline\n        random_preds = random_baseline(len(disagreements))\n\n        # Confidence baseline\n        conf_preds = confidence_baseline(disagreements)\n\n        # Trust score baseline\n        trust_preds = trust_score_baseline(disagreements, train_texts, train_labels)\n\n        # Directional rule\n        dir_preds = []\n        for d in disagreements:\n            if d['pred_simple'] == majority_class:\n                dir_preds.append(d['pred_simple'])\n            else:\n                dir_preds.append(d['pred_complex'])\n\n        # True labels for disagreements\n        true_labels_d = [d['true_label'] for d in disagreements]\n\n        # Compute metrics\n        dir_accuracy = accuracy_score(true_labels_d, dir_preds)\n        conf_accuracy = accuracy_score(true_labels_d, conf_preds)\n        trust_accuracy = accuracy_score(true_labels_d, trust_preds)\n        random_accuracy = accuracy_score(true_labels_d, random_preds)\n\n        # Statistical tests\n        _, dir_pvalue = binomial_test_on_directional_rule(disagreements, majority_class)\n\n        # McNemar's tests between directional rule and baselines\n        _, mcnemar_conf_pvalue = mcnemar_test(true_labels_d, dir_preds, conf_preds)\n        _, mcnemar_trust_pvalue = mcnemar_test(true_labels_d, dir_preds, trust_preds)\n        _, mcnemar_random_pvalue = mcnemar_test(true_labels_d, dir_preds, random_preds)\n\n    else:\n        dir_accuracy = conf_accuracy = trust_accuracy = random_accuracy = 0.0\n        dir_pvalue = mcnemar_conf_pvalue = mcnemar_trust_pvalue = mcnemar_random_pvalue = 1.0\n        dir_preds = conf_preds = trust_preds = random_preds = []\n\n    # Overall accuracies\n    simple_accuracy = accuracy_score(test_labels, simple_preds)\n    complex_accuracy = accuracy_score(test_labels, complex_preds)\n\n    result = {\n        'dataset': dataset_name,\n        'sample_size': sample_size,\n        'imbalance_ratio': imbalance_ratio,\n        'seed': seed,\n        'train_size': len(train_texts),\n        'test_size': len(test_texts),\n        'simple_accuracy': float(simple_accuracy),\n        'complex_accuracy': float(complex_accuracy),\n        'num_disagreements': len(disagreements),\n        'disagreement_ratio': len(disagreements) / len(test_texts) if len(test_texts) > 0 else 0,\n        'majority_class': complex_model.predict_proba(test_texts)\n\n    # Find disagreements\n    disagreements = []\n    for i, (text, true_label) in enumerate(zip(test_texts, test_labels)):\n        if simple_preds[i] != i\n            })\n\n    logger.debug(f\"Found {len(disagreements)} disagreements out of {len(test_texts)} test samples\")\n\n    # Compute baselines on disagreement set\n    if len(disagreements) > score baseline\n        trust_preds = trust_score_baseline(disagreements, train_texts, train_labels)\n\n        # Directional rule\n        dir_preds = []\n        for d in disagreements:\n            if d['pred_simple'] == majority_class:\n                dir_preds.append(d['pred_simple'])\n            else:\n                dir_preds.append(d['pred_complex'])\n\n        # True labels for    }\n\n    return summary\n\n\ndef save_results(results: list[dict], ablation: dict):\n    \"\"\"Save results to JSON files.\"\"\"\n    # Main output\n    output = {\n        'metadata': {\n {mean_trust_acc:.3f}\")\n    print(f\"Mean random baseline accuracy: {mean_rand_acc:.3f}\")\n    print(\"=\"*60 + \"\\n\")\n\n    logger.info(\"Experiment completed successfully\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n", "new_content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Disagreement Direction Test for Sentiment Classification.\n\nCompares TF-IDF Logistic Regression vs character n-gram RandomForest\non small sentiment datasets, analyzing whether disagreement direction\npredicts the correct label better than chance and concrete baselines.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport gc\nimport json\nimport math\nimport multiprocessing as mp\nimport os\nimport resource\nimport sys\nimport time\nfrom collections import Counter\nfrom concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor, as_completed\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Any\n\nimport numpy as np\nfrom datasets import load_dataset\nfrom loguru import logger\nfrom scipy.stats import binomtest\nfrom sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier\nfrom sklearn.feature_extraction.text import CountVectorizer, TfidfVectorizer\nfrom sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression\nfrom sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score\nfrom sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split\nfrom sklearn.neighbors import NearestNeighbors\nfrom sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline\n\n# ============================================================================\n# CONFIGURATION AND CONSTANTS\n# ============================================================================\n\nWORKSPACE = Path(\n    \"/ai-inventor/aii_data/runs/run_q27XJGeAT3TE/3_invention_loop/iter_1/gen_art/gen_art_experiment_1\"\n)\nLOG_DIR = WORKSPACE / \"logs\"\nOUTPUT_DIR = WORKSPACE / \"results\"\nLOG_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)\nOUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)\n\nDATASETS = [\"sst2\", \"imdb\"]\nSAMPLE_SIZES = [100, 200, 500, 1000]\nIMBALANCE_RATIOS = [0.5, 0.7, 0.9]  # majority:minority ratio\nSEEDS = list(range(10))\nNUM_WORKERS = 2  # Container has 2 CPUs\n\n# Memory limits based on container resources (14GB RAM)\nRAM_BUDGET = 12 * 1024**3  # 12GB\n\n# ============================================================================\n# LOGGING SETUP\n# ============================================================================\n\nlogger.remove()\nlogger.add(\n    sys.stdout,\n    level=\"INFO\",\n    format=\"{time:HH:mm:ss}|{level:<7}|{message}\",\n)\nlogger.add(\n    LOG_DIR / \"run.log\",\n    rotation=\"30 MB\",\n    level=\"DEBUG\",\n)\n\n# ============================================================================\n# HARDWARE DETECTION\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef _detect_cpus() -> int:\n    \"\"\"Detect actual CPU allocation (containers/pods/bare metal).\"\"\"\n    try:  # cgroups v2 quota\n        parts = Path(\"/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.max\").read_text().split()\n        if parts[0] != \"max\":\n            return max(1, math.ceil(int(parts[0]) / int(parts[1])))\n    except (FileNotFoundError, ValueError):\n        pass\n    try:  # cgroups v1 quota\n        q = int(Path(\"/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/cpu.cfs_quota_us\").read_text())\n        p = int(Path(\"/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/cpu.cfs_period_us\").read_text())\n        if q > 0:\n            return max(1, math.ceil(q / p))\n    except (FileNotFoundError, ValueError):\n        pass\n    try:  # CPU affinity (cpuset \u2014 used by RunPod, Docker --cpuset-cpus)\n        return len(os.sched_getaffinity(0))\n    except (AttributeError, OSError):\n        pass\n    return os.cpu_count() or 1\n\nNUM_CPUS = _detect_cpus()\nlogger.info(f\"Detected {NUM_CPUS} CPUs\")\n\n# Set memory limits\nresource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_AS, (RAM_BUDGET * 3, RAM_BUDGET * 3))\n\n# ============================================================================\n# MODEL DEFINITIONS\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef get_simple_model():\n    \"\"\"Simple model: TF-IDF + Logistic Regression.\"\"\"\n    return Pipeline([\n        ('tfidf', TfidfVectorizer(max_features=10000, ngram_range=(1, 2))),\n        ('clf', LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000, random_state=42, n_jobs=1))\n    ])\n\n\ndef get_complex_model():\n    \"\"\"Complex model: character n-grams + RandomForest.\"\"\"\n    return Pipeline([\n        ('char_ngram', CountVectorizer(\n            analyzer='char',\n            ngram_range=(3, 5),\n            max_features=20000\n        )),\n        ('clf', RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=100, random_state=42, n_jobs=1))\n    ])\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# DATA LOADING AND PREPARATION\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef load_sst2():\n    \"\"\"Load SST-2 dataset.\"\"\"\n    logger.info(\"Loading SST-2 dataset\")\n    ds = load_dataset(\"stanfordnlp/sst2\", split=\"train\")\n    texts = ds[\"sentence\"]\n    labels = ds[\"label\"]\n    del ds\n    gc.collect()\n    return texts, labels\n\n\ndef load_imdb():\n    \"\"\"Load IMDB dataset.\"\"\"\n    logger.info(\"Loading IMDB dataset\")\n    ds = load_dataset(\"stanfordnlp/imdb\", split=\"train\")\n    texts = ds[\"text\"]\n    labels = ds[\"label\"]\n    del ds\n    gc.collect()\n    return texts, labels\n\n\ndef stratified_imbalanced_subsample(\n    texts: list[str],\n    labels: list[int],\n    target_size: int,\n    imbalance_ratio: float,\n    random_state: int\n) -> tuple[list[str], list[int]]:\n    \"\"\"Create a stratified subsample with controlled class imbalance.\n\n    Args:\n        texts: List of text samples\n        labels: List of labels\n        target_size: Total target sample size\n        imbalance_ratio: Ratio of majority to minority class (0.5 = balanced)\n        random_state: Random seed\n\n    Returns:\n        Subsampled texts and labels\n    \"\"\"\n    rng = np.random.RandomState(random_state)\n\n    # Separate by class\n    class_0_idx = [i for i, l in enumerate(labels) if l == 0]\n    class_1_idx = [i for i, l in enumerate(labels) if l == 1]\n\n    # Calculate sizes based on imbalance ratio\n    # imbalance_ratio = majority_size / minority_size\n    # total = majority_size + minority_size\n    minority_size = int(target_size / (1 + imbalance_ratio))\n    majority_size = target_size - minority_size\n\n    # Sample from each class\n    sampled_0 = rng.choice(class_0_idx, size=min(majority_size, len(class_0_idx)), replace=False)\n    sampled_1 = rng.choice(class_1_idx, size=min(minority_size, len(class_1_idx)), replace=False)\n\n    # Combine and shuffle\n    indices = np.concatenate([sampled_0, sampled_1])\n    rng.shuffle(indices)\n\n    return [texts[i] for i in indices], [labels[i] for i in indices]\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# BASELINE METHODS\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef confidence_baseline(disagreements: list[dict]) -> list[int]:\n    \"\"\"Baseline: predict whichever model has higher confidence.\"\"\"\n    predictions = []\n    for d in disagreements:\n        if d['prob_simple'] > d['prob_complex']:\n            predictions.append(d['pred_simple'])\n        else:\n            predictions.append(d['pred_complex'])\n    return predictions\n\n\ndef trust_score_baseline(disagreements: list[dict], train_texts: list[str], train_labels: list[int]) -> list[int]:\n    \"\"\"Baseline: trust-score style proxy using nearest-neighbor agreement.\"\"\"\n    # Build TF-IDF representation of training data\n    vectorizer = TfidfVectorizer(max_features=10000, ngram_range=(1, 2))\n    try:\n        train_tfidf = vectorizer.fit_transform(train_texts)\n        nn = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=5, metric='cosine')\n        nn.fit(train_tfidf)\n\n        predictions = []\n        for d in disagreements:\n            # Transform test text\n            test_vec = vectorizer.transform([d['text']])\n            distances, indices = nn.kneighbors(test_vec)\n            neighbor_labels = [train_labels[i] for i in indices[0]]\n            majority_label = Counter(neighbor_labels).most_common(1)[0][0]\n            predictions.append(majority_label)\n    except Exception as e:\n        logger.warning(f\"Trust score baseline failed: {e}\")\n        # Fallback to random\n        predictions = [np.random.choice([0, 1]) for _ in disagreements]\n\n    return predictions\n\n\ndef random_baseline(n: int) -> list[int]:\n    \"\"\"Random baseline.\"\"\"\n    return np.random.RandomState(42).randint(0, 2, size=n).tolist()\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# STATISTICAL TESTS\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef binomial_test_on_directional_rule(disagreements: list[dict], majority_class: int) -> tuple[float, float]:\n    \"\"\"Test if directional rule accuracy > 50% using binomial test.\"\"\"\n    correct = sum(\n        1 for d in disagreements\n        if (d['pred_simple'] == majority_class and d['pred_simple'] == d['true_label']) or\n           (d['pred_simple'] != majority_class and d['pred_complex'] == d['true_label'])\n    )\n    n = len(disagreements)\n    if n == 0:\n        return 0.0, 1.0\n    p_value = binom_test(correct, n, 0.5, alternative='greater')\n    accuracy = correct / n\n    return accuracy, p_value\n\n\ndef mcnemar_test(y_true: list[int], pred1: list[int], pred2: list[int]) -> tuple[float, float]:\n    \"\"\"McNemar's test between two prediction sets.\"\"\"\n    # Contingency table\n    a = sum(1 for yt, p1, p2 in zip(y_true, pred1, pred2)\n            if p1 == yt and p2 != yt)  # pred1 correct, pred2 wrong\n    b = sum(1 for yt, p1, p2 in zip(y_true, pred1, pred2)\n            if p1 != yt and p2 == yt)  # pred1 wrong, pred2 correct\n    c = sum(1 for yt, p1, p2 in zip(y_true, pred1, pred2)\n            if p1 != yt and p2 != yt)  # both wrong\n    d = sum(1 for yt, p1, p2 in zip(y_true, pred1, pred2)\n            if p1 == yt and p2 == yt)  # both correct\n\n    # McNemar's test on discordant pairs\n    if a + b == 0:\n        return 0.0, 1.0\n\n    # Use binomial approximation for McNemar's test\n    # For larger samples, chi-square with continuity correction\n    if a + b < 25:\n        p_value = binom_test(a, a + b, 0.5, alternative='two-sided')\n    else:\n        chi2 = (abs(a - b) - 1) ** 2 / (a + b)\n        p_value = stats.chi2.sf(chi2, 1)\n\n    accuracy1 = (a + d) / len(y_true) if len(y_true) > 0 else 0\n    accuracy2 = (b + d) / len(y_true) if len(y_true) > 0 else 0\n\n    return accuracy1, p_value\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# EXPERIMENT EXECUTION\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef run_single_experiment(\n    dataset_name: str,\n    texts: list[str],\n    labels: list[int],\n    sample_size: int,\n    imbalance_ratio: float,\n    seed: int\n) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"Run a single experiment configuration.\"\"\"\n    logger.info(\n        f\"Running: dataset={dataset_name}, size={sample_size}, \"\n        f\"imbalance={imbalance_ratio}, seed={seed}\"\n    )\n\n    # Subsample\n    sub_texts, sub_labels = stratified_imbalanced_subsample(\n        texts, labels, sample_size, imbalance_ratio, seed\n    )\n\n    # Determine majority class\n    majority_class = Counter(sub_labels).most_common(1)[0][0]\n    logger.debug(f\"Majority class: {majority_class}, distribution: {Counter(sub_labels)}\")\n\n    # Train/test split (80/20), stratified\n    train_texts, test_texts, train_labels, test_labels = train_test_split(\n        sub_texts, sub_labels, test_size=0.2, random_state=seed, stratify=sub_labels\n    )\n\n    # Fit simple model\n    simple_model = get_simple_model()\n    simple_model.fit(train_texts, train_labels)\n    simple_preds = simple_model.predict(test_texts)\n    simple_probs = simple_model.predict_proba(test_texts)\n\n    # Fit complex model\n    complex_model = get_complex_model()\n    complex_model.fit(train_texts, train_labels)\n    complex_preds = complex_model.predict(test_texts)\n    complex_probs = complex_model.predict_proba(test_texts)\n\n    # Find disagreements\n    disagreements = []\n    for i, (text, true_label) in enumerate(zip(test_texts, test_labels)):\n        if simple_preds[i] != yt)  # pred1 correct, pred2 wrong\n    b = sum(1 for yt, p1, p2 in zip(y_true, pred1, pred2)\n            if p1 != yt and p2 == yt)  # pred1 wrong, pred2 correct\n    c = sum(1 for yt, p1, p2 in zip(y_true, pred1, pred2)\n            if p1 != yt and p2 != yt)  # both wrong\n    d = sum(1 for yt, p1, p2 in zip(y_true, pred1, pred2)\n            if p1 == yt and p2 == yt)  # both correct\n\n    # McNemar's test on discordant pairs\n    if a + b == 0:\n        return 0.0, 1.0\n\n    # Use binomial approximation for McNemar's test\n    # For larger samples, chi-square with continuity correction\n    if a + b < 25:\n        p_value = binom_test(a, a + b, 0.5, alternative='two-sided')\n    else:\n        chi2 = (abs(a - b) - 1) ** 2 / (a + b)\n        p_value = stats.chi2.sf(chi2, 1)\n\n    accuracy1 = (a + d) / len(y_true) if len(y_true) > 0 else 0\n    accuracy2 = (b + d) / len(y_true) if len(y_true) > 0 else 0\n\n    return accuracy1, p_value\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# EXPERIMENT EXECUTION\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef run_single_experiment(\n    dataset_name: str,\n    texts: list[str],\n    labels: list[int],\n    sample_size: int,\n    imbalance_ratio: float,\n    seed: int\n) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"Run a single experiment configuration.\"\"\"\n    logger.info(\n        f\"Running: dataset={dataset_name}, size={sample_size}, \"\n        f\"imbalance={imbalance_ratio}, seed={seed}\"\n    )\n\n    # Subsample\n    sub_texts, sub_labels = stratified_imbalanced_subsample(\n        texts, labels, sample_size, imbalance_ratio, seed\n    )\n\n    # Determine majority class\n    majority_class = Counter(sub_labels).most_common(1)[0][0]\n    logger.debug(f\"Majority class: {majority_class}, distribution: {Counter(sub_labels)}\")\n\n    # Train/test split (80/20), stratified\n    train_texts, test_texts, train_labels, test_labels = train_test_split(\n        sub_texts, sub_labels, test_size=0.2, random_state=seed, stratify=sub_labels\n    )\n\n    # Fit simple model\n    simple_model = get_simple_model()\n    simple_model.fit(train_texts, train_labels)\n    simple_preds = simple_model.predict(test_texts)\n    simple_probs = simple_model.predict_proba(test_texts)\n\n    # Fit complex model\n    complex_model = get_complex_model()\n    complex_model.fit(train_texts, train_labels)\n    complex_preds = complex_model.predict(test_texts)\n    complex_probs = complex_model.predict_proba(test_texts)\n\n    # Find disagreements\n    disagreements = []\n    for i, (text, true_label) in enumerate(zip(test_texts, test_labels)):\n        if simple_preds[i] != complex_preds[i]:\n            disagreements.append({\n                'text': text,\n                'true_label': int(true_label),\n                'pred_simple': int(simple_preds[i]),\n                'pred_complex': int(complex_preds[i]),\n                'prob_simple': float(max(simple_probs[i])),\n                'prob_complex': float(max(complex_probs[i])),\n                'sample_index': i\n            })\n\n    logger.debug(f\"Found {len(disagreements)} disagreements out of {len(test_texts)} test samples\")\n\n    # Compute baselines on disagreement set\n    if len(disagreements) > 0:\n        # Random baseline\n        random_preds = random_baseline(len(disagreements))\n\n        # Confidence baseline\n        conf_preds = confidence_baseline(disagreements)\n\n        # Trust score baseline\n        trust_preds = trust_score_baseline(disagreements, train_texts, train_labels)\n\n        # Directional rule\n        dir_preds = []\n        for d in disagreements:\n            if d['pred_simple'] == majority_class:\n                dir_preds.append(d['pred_simple'])\n            else:\n                dir_preds.append(d['pred_complex'])\n\n        # True labels for disagreements\n        true_labels_d = [d['true_label'] for d in disagreements]\n\n        # Compute metrics\n        dir_accuracy = accuracy_score(true_labels_d, dir_preds)\n        conf_accuracy = accuracy_score(true_labels_d, conf_preds)\n        trust_accuracy = accuracy_score(true_labels_d, trust_preds)\n        random_accuracy = accuracy_score(true_labels_d, random_preds)\n\n        # Statistical tests\n        _, dir_pvalue = binomial_test_on_directional_rule(disagreements, majority_class)\n\n        # McNemar's tests between directional rule and baselines\n        _, mcnemar_conf_pvalue = mcnemar_test(true_labels_d, dir_preds, conf_preds)\n        _, mcnemar_trust_pvalue = mcnemar_test(true_labels_d, dir_preds, trust_preds)\n        _, mcnemar_random_pvalue = mcnemar_test(true_labels_d, dir_preds, random_preds)\n\n    else:\n        dir_accuracy = conf_accuracy = trust_accuracy = random_accuracy = 0.0\n        dir_pvalue = mcnemar_conf_pvalue = mcnemar_trust_pvalue = mcnemar_random_pvalue = 1.0\n        dir_preds = conf_preds = trust_preds = random_preds = []\n\n    # Overall accuracies\n    simple_accuracy = accuracy_score(test_labels, simple_preds)\n    complex_accuracy = accuracy_score(test_labels, complex_preds)\n\n    result = {\n        'dataset': dataset_name,\n        'sample_size': sample_size,\n        'imbalance_ratio': imbalance_ratio,\n        'seed': seed,\n        'train_size': len(train_texts),\n        'test_size': len(test_texts),\n        'simple_accuracy': float(simple_accuracy),\n        'complex_accuracy': float(complex_accuracy),\n        'num_disagreements': len(disagreements),\n        'disagreement_ratio': len(disagreements) / len(test_texts) if len(test_texts) > 0 else 0,\n        'majority_class': int(majority_class),\n        'class_distribution': dict(Counter(sub_labels)),\n        'directional_rule_accuracy': float(dir_accuracy),\n        'confidence_baseline_accuracy': float(conf_accuracy),\n        'trust_score_baseline_accuracy': float(trust_accuracy),\n        'random_baseline_accuracy': float(random_accuracy),\n        'directional_rule_pvalue': float(dir_pvalue),\n        'mcnemar_vs_confidence_pvalue': float(mcnemar_conf_pvalue),\n        'mcnemar_vs_trust_score_pvalue': float(mcnemar_trust_pvalue),\n        'mcnemar_vs_random_pvalue': float(mcnemar_random_pvalue),\n    }\n\n    logger.info(\n        f\"Completed: size={sample_size}, seed={seed}, \"\n        f\"disagreements={len(disagreements)}, dir_acc={dir_accuracy:.3f}\"\n    )\n\n    return result\n\n\ndef run_all_experiments() -> list[dict[str, Any]]:\n    \"\"\"Run all experiment configurations.\"\"\"\n    logger.info(\"Starting all experiments\")\n\n    # Load datasets\n    sst2_texts, sst2_labels = load_sst2()\n    imdb_texts, imdb_labels = load_imdb()\n\n    dataset_map = {\n        'sst2': (sst2_texts, sst2_labels),\n        'imdb': (imdb_texts, imdb_labels)\n    }\n\n    all_results = []\n\n    # Generate all configurations\n    configs = []\n    for dataset_name in DATASETS:\n        texts, labels = dataset_map[dataset_name]\n        for texts, labels,\n                        sample_size, imbalance_ratio, seed\n                    ))\n\n    logger.info(f\"Total configurations: {len(configs)}\")\n\n    # Run in parallel with ProcessPoolExecutor\n    # Use spawn context to avoid loguru deadlock issues\n    mp_context = mp.get_context(\"spawn\")\n    with ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=NUM_WORKERS, mp_context=mp_context)          config = futures[future]\n            try:\n                result = future.result()\n                all_results.append(result)\n            except Exception as e:\n  all_results.append({\n                    'dataset': dataset_name,\n                    'sample_size': sample_size,\n                    'imbalance_ratio': imbalance_ratio,\n    }\n\n    return summary\n\n\ndef save_results(results: list[dict], ablation: dict):\n    \"\"\"Save results to JSON files.\"\"\"\n    # Main output\n    output = {\n        'metadata': {\n      dataset_name='sst2',\n            texts=['sample text 1', 'sample text 2'] * 50,  # Dummy data for quick test\n            labels=[0, 1] * 50,\n            sample_size=100,\n in result\n\n        logger.info(\"Smoke test passed\")\n        return True\n\n    except Exception as e:\n        logger.error(f\"Smoke test failed: {e}\")\n        return False\n\n\n#    print(f\"Mean directional rule accuracy: {mean_dir_acc:.3f}\")\n    print(f\"Mean confidence baseline accuracy: {mean_conf_acc:.3f}\")\n    print(f\"Mean trust score baseline accuracy: {mean_trust_acc:.3f}\")\n    print(f\"Mean random baseline accuracy: {mean_rand_acc:.3f}\")\n    print(\"=\"*60 + \"\\n\")\n\n    logger.info(\"Experiment completed successfully\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n", "new_content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Disagreement Direction Test for Sentiment Classification.\n\nCompares TF-IDF Logistic Regression vs character n-gram RandomForest\non small sentiment datasets, analyzing whether disagreement direction\npredicts the correct label better than chance and concrete baselines.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport gc\nimport json\nimport math\nimport multiprocessing as mp\nimport os\nimport resource\nimport sys\nimport time\nfrom collections import Counter\nfrom concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor, as_completed\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Any\n\nimport numpy as np\nfrom datasets import load_dataset\nfrom loguru import logger\nfrom scipy.stats import binomtest\nfrom sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier\nfrom sklearn.feature_extraction.text import CountVectorizer, TfidfVectorizer\nfrom sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression\nfrom sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score\nfrom sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split\nfrom sklearn.neighbors import NearestNeighbors\nfrom sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline\n\n# ============================================================================\n# CONFIGURATION AND CONSTANTS\n# ============================================================================\n\nWORKSPACE = Path(\n    \"/ai-inventor/aii_data/runs/run_q27XJGeAT3TE/3_invention_loop/iter_1/gen_art/gen_art_experiment_1\"\n)\nLOG_DIR = WORKSPACE / \"logs\"\nOUTPUT_DIR = WORKSPACE / \"results\"\nLOG_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)\nOUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)\n\nDATASETS = [\"sst2\", \"imdb\"]\nSAMPLE_SIZES = [100, 200, 500, 1000]\nIMBALANCE_RATIOS = [0.5, 0.7, 0.9]  # majority:minority ratio\nSEEDS = list(range(10))\nNUM_WORKERS = 2  # Container has 2 CPUs\n\n# Memory limits based on container resources (14GB RAM)\nRAM_BUDGET = 12 * 1024**3  # 12GB\n\n# ============================================================================\n# LOGGING SETUP\n# ============================================================================\n\nlogger.remove()\nlogger.add(\n    sys.stdout,\n    level=\"INFO\",\n    format=\"{time:HH:mm:ss}|{level:<7}|{message}\",\n)\nlogger.add(\n    LOG_DIR / \"run.log\",\n    rotation=\"30 MB\",\n    level=\"DEBUG\",\n)\n\n# ============================================================================\n# HARDWARE DETECTION\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef _detect_cpus() -> int:\n    \"\"\"Detect actual CPU allocation (containers/pods/bare metal).\"\"\"\n    try:  # cgroups v2 quota\n        parts = Path(\"/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.max\").read_text().split()\n        if parts[0] != \"max\":\n            return max(1, math.ceil(int(parts[0]) / int(parts[1])))\n    except (FileNotFoundError, ValueError):\n        pass\n    try:  # cgroups v1 quota\n        q = int(Path(\"/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/cpu.cfs_quota_us\").read_text())\n        p = int(Path(\"/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/cpu.cfs_period_us\").read_text())\n        if q > 0:\n            return max(1, math.ceil(q / p))\n    except (FileNotFoundError, ValueError):\n        pass\n    try:  # CPU affinity (cpuset \u2014 used by RunPod, Docker --cpuset-cpus)\n        return len(os.sched_getaffinity(0))\n    except (AttributeError, OSError):\n        pass\n    return os.cpu_count() or 1\n\nNUM_CPUS = _detect_cpus()\nlogger.info(f\"Detected {NUM_CPUS} CPUs\")\n\n# Set memory limits\nresource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_AS, (RAM_BUDGET * 3, RAM_BUDGET * 3))\n\n# ============================================================================\n# MODEL DEFINITIONS\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef get_simple_model():\n    \"\"\"Simple model: TF-IDF + Logistic Regression.\"\"\"\n    return Pipeline([\n        ('tfidf', TfidfVectorizer(max_features=10000, ngram_range=(1, 2))),\n        ('clf', LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000, random_state=42, n_jobs=1))\n    ])\n\n\ndef get_complex_model():\n    \"\"\"Complex model: character n-grams + RandomForest.\"\"\"\n    return Pipeline([\n        ('char_ngram', CountVectorizer(\n            analyzer='char',\n            ngram_range=(3, 5),\n            max_features=20000\n        )),\n        ('clf', RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=100, random_state=42, n_jobs=1))\n    ])\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# DATA LOADING AND PREPARATION\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef load_sst2():\n    \"\"\"Load SST-2 dataset.\"\"\"\n    logger.info(\"Loading SST-2 dataset\")\n    ds = load_dataset(\"stanfordnlp/sst2\", split=\"train\")\n    texts = ds[\"sentence\"]\n    labels = ds[\"label\"]\n    del ds\n    gc.collect()\n    return texts, labels\n\n\ndef load_imdb():\n    \"\"\"Load IMDB dataset.\"\"\"\n    logger.info(\"Loading IMDB dataset\")\n    ds = load_dataset(\"stanfordnlp/imdb\", split=\"train\")\n    texts = ds[\"text\"]\n    labels = ds[\"label\"]\n    del ds\n    gc.collect()\n    return texts, labels\n\n\ndef stratified_imbalanced_subsample(\n    texts: list[str],\n    labels: list[int],\n    target_size: int,\n    imbalance_ratio: float,\n    random_state: int\n) -> tuple[list[str], list[int]]:\n    \"\"\"Create a stratified subsample with controlled class imbalance.\n\n    Args:\n        texts: List of text samples\n        labels: List of labels\n        target_size: Total target sample size\n        imbalance_ratio: Ratio of majority to minority class (0.5 = balanced)\n        random_state: Random seed\n\n    Returns:\n        Subsampled texts and labels\n    \"\"\"\n    rng = np.random.RandomState(random_state)\n\n    # Separate by class\n    class_0_idx = [i for i, l in enumerate(labels) if l == 0]\n    class_1_idx = [i for i, l in enumerate(labels) if l == 1]\n\n    # Calculate sizes based on imbalance ratio\n    # imbalance_ratio = majority_size / minority_size\n    # total = majority_size + minority_size\n    minority_size = int(target_size / (1 + imbalance_ratio))\n    majority_size = target_size - minority_size\n\n    # Sample from each class\n    sampled_0 = rng.choice(class_0_idx, size=min(majority_size, len(class_0_idx)), replace=False)\n    sampled_1 = rng.choice(class_1_idx, size=min(minority_size, len(class_1_idx)), replace=False)\n\n    # Combine and shuffle\n    indices = np.concatenate([sampled_0, sampled_1])\n    rng.shuffle(indices)\n\n    return [texts[i] for i in indices], [labels[i] for i in indices]\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# BASELINE METHODS\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef confidence_baseline(disagreements: list[dict]) -> list[int]:\n    \"\"\"Baseline: predict whichever model has higher confidence.\"\"\"\n    predictions = []\n    for d in disagreements:\n        if d['prob_simple'] > d['prob_complex']:\n            predictions.append(d['pred_simple'])\n        else:\n            predictions.append(d['pred_complex'])\n    return predictions\n\n\ndef trust_score_baseline(disagreements: list[dict], train_texts: list[str], train_labels: list[int]) -> list[int]:\n    \"\"\"Baseline: trust-score style proxy using nearest-neighbor agreement.\"\"\"\n    # Build TF-IDF representation of training data\n    vectorizer = TfidfVectorizer(max_features=10000, ngram_range=(1, 2))\n    try:\n        train_tfidf = vectorizer.fit_transform(train_texts)\n        nn = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=5, metric='cosine')\n        nn.fit(train_tfidf)\n\n        predictions = []\n        for d in disagreements:\n            # Transform test text\n            test_vec = vectorizer.transform([d['text']])\n            distances, indices = nn.kneighbors(test_vec)\n            neighbor_labels = [train_labels[i] for i in indices[0]]\n            majority_label = Counter(neighbor_labels).most_common(1)[0][0]\n            predictions.append(majority_label)\n    except Exception as e:\n        logger.warning(f\"Trust score baseline failed: {e}\")\n        # Fallback to random\n        predictions = [np.random.choice([0, 1]) for _ in disagreements]\n\n    return predictions\n\n\ndef random_baseline(n: int) -> list[int]:\n    \"\"\"Random baseline.\"\"\"\n    return np.random.RandomState(42).randint(0, 2, size=n).tolist()\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# STATISTICAL TESTS\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef binomial_test_on_directional_rule(disagreements: list[dict], majority_class: int) -> tuple[float, float]:\n    \"\"\"Test if directional rule accuracy > 50% using binomial test.\"\"\"\n    correct = sum(\n        1 for d in disagreements\n        if (d['pred_simple'] == majority_class and d['pred_simple'] == d['true_label']) or\n           (d['pred_simple'] != majority_class and d['pred_complex'] == d['true_label'])\n    )\n    n = len(disagreements)\n    if n == 0:\n        return 0.0, 1.0\n    result = binomtest(correct, n, 0.5, alternative='greater')\n    p_value = result.pvalue\n    accuracy = correct / n\n    return accuracy, p_value\n\n\ndef mcnemar_test(y_true: list[int], pred1: list[int], pred2: list[int]) -> tuple[float, float]:\n    \"\"\"McNemar's test between two prediction sets.\"\"\"\n    # Contingency table\n    a = sum(1 for yt, p1, p2 in zip(y_true, pred1, pred2)\n for yt, p1, p2 in zip(y_true, pred1, pred2)\n            if p1 != yt and p2 != yt)  # both wrong\n    d = sum(1 for yt, p1, p2 in zip(y_true, pred1, pred2)\n            if p1 == yt and p2 == yt)  # ngram_range=(1, 2))\n    try:\n        train_tfidf = vectorizer.fit_transform(train_texts)\n        nn = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=5, metric='cosine')\n        nn.fit(train_tfidf)\n\n        predictions = []\n        for d in disagreements:\n            # Transform test text\n            test_vec = vectorizer.transform([d['text']])\n            distances, indices = nn.kneighbors(test_vec)\n            neighbor_labels = [train_labels[i] for i in indices[0]]\n            majority_label = Counter(neighbor_labels).most_common(1)[0][0]\n            predictions.append(majority_label)\n    except Exception as e:\n        logger.warning(f\"Trust score baseline failed: {e}\")\n        # Fallback to random\n        predictions = [np.random.choice([0, 1]) for _ in disagreements]\n\n    return predictions\n\n\ndef random_baseline(n: int) -> list[int]:\n    \"\"\"Random baseline.\"\"\"\n    return np.random.RandomState(42).randint(0, 2, size=n).tolist()\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# STATISTICAL TESTS\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef binomial_test_on_directional_rule(disagreements: list[dict], majority_class: int) -> tuple[float, float]:\n    \"\"\"Test if directional rule accuracy > 50% using binomial test.\"\"\"\n    correct = sum(\n        1 for d in disagreements\n        if (d['pred_simple'] == majority_class and d['pred_simple'] == d['true_label']) or\n           (d['pred_simple'] != majority_class and d['pred_complex'] == d['true_label'])\n    )\n    n = len(disagreements)\n    if n == 0:\n        return 0.0, 1.0\n    result = binomtest(correct, n, 0.5, alternative='greater')\n    p_value = result.pvalue\n    accuracy = correct / n\n    return accuracy, p_value\n\n\ndef mcnemar_test(y_true: list[int], pred1: list[int], pred2: list[int]) -> tuple[float, float]:\n    \"\"\"McNemar's test between two prediction sets.\"\"\"\n    # Contingency table\n    a = sum(1 for yt, p1, p2 in zip(y_true, pred1, pred2)\n            if p1 == yt and p2 != yt)  # pred1 correct, pred2 wrong\n    b = sum(1 for yt, p1, p2 in zip(y_true, pred1, pred2)\n            if p1 != yt and p2 == yt)  # pred1 wrong, pred2 correct\n    c = sum(1 for yt, p1, p2 in zip(y_true, pred1, pred2)\n            if p1 != yt and p2 != yt)  # both wrong\n    d = sum(1 for yt, p1, p2 in zip(y_true, pred1, pred2)\n            if p1 == yt and p2 == yt)  # both correct\n\n    # McNemar's test on discordant pairs\n    if a + b == 0:\n        return 0.0, 1.0\n\n    # Use binomial approximation for McNemar's test\n    # For larger samples, chi-square with continuity correction\n    if a + b < 25:\n        p_value = binom_test(a, a + b, 0.5, alternative='two-sided')\n    else:\n        chi2 = (abs(a - b) - 1) ** 2 / (a + b)\n        p_value = stats.chi2.sf(chi2, 1)\n\n    accuracy1 = (a + d) / len(y_true) if len(y_true) > 0 else 0\n    accuracy2 = (b + d) / len(y_true) if len(y_true) > 0 else 0\n\n    return accuracy1, p_value\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# EXPERIMENT EXECUTION\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef run_single_experiment(\n    dataset_name: str,\n    texts: list[str],\n    labels: list[int],\n    sample_size: int,\n    imbalance_ratio: float,\n    seed: int\n) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"Run a single experiment configuration.\"\"\"\n    logger.info(\n        f\"Running: dataset={dataset_name}, size={sample_size}, \"\n        f\"imbalance={imbalance_ratio}, seed={seed}\"\n    )\n\n    # Subsample\n    sub_texts, sub_labels = stratified_imbalanced_subsample(\n        texts, labels, sample_size, imbalance_ratio, seed\n    )\n\n    # Determine majority class\n    majority_class = Counter(sub_labels).most_common(1)[0][0]\n    logger.debug(f\"Majority class: {majority_class}, distribution: {Counter(sub_labels)}\")\n\n    # Train/test split (80/20), stratified\n    train_texts, test_texts, train_labels, test_labels = train_test_split(\n        sub_texts, sub_labels, test_size=0.2, random_state=seed, stratify=sub_labels\n    )\n\n    # Fit simple model\n    simple_model = get_simple_model()\n    simple_model.fit(train_texts, train_labels)\n    simple_preds = simple_model.predict(test_texts)\n    simple_probs = simple_model.predict_proba(test_texts)\n\n    # Fit complex model\n    complex_model = get_complex_model()\n    complex_model.fit(train_texts, train_labels)\n    complex_preds = complex_model.predict(test_texts)\n    complex_probs = complex_model.predict_proba(test_texts)\n\n    # Find disagreements\n    disagreements = []\n    for i, (text, true_label) in enumerate(zip(test_texts, test_labels)):\n        if simple_preds[i] != complex_preds[i]:\n            disagreements.append({\n                'text': text,\n                'true_label': int(true_label),\n                'pred_simple': int(simple_preds[i]),\n                'pred_complex': int(complex_preds[i]),\n                'prob_simple': float(max(simple_probs[i])),\n                'prob_complex': float(max(complex_probs[i])),\n                'sample_index': i\n            })\n\n    logger.debug(f\"Found {len(disagreements)} disagreements out of {len(test_texts)} test samples\")\n\n    # Compute baselines on disagreement set\n    if len(disagreements) > 0:\n        # Random baseline\n        random_preds = random_baseline(len(disagreements))\n\n        # Confidence baseline\n        conf_preds = confidence_baseline(disagreements)\n\n        # Trust score baseline\n        trust_preds = trust_score_baseline(disagreements, train_texts, train_labels)\n\n        # Directional rule\n        dir_preds = []\n        for d in disagreements:\n            if d['pred_simple'] == majority_class:\n                dir_preds.append(d['pred_simple'])\n            else:\n                dir_preds.append(d['pred_complex'])\n\n        # True labels for disagreements\n        true_labels_d = [d['true_label'] for d in disagreements]\n\n        # Compute metrics\n        dir_accuracy = accuracy_score(true_labels_d, dir_preds)\n        conf_accuracy = accuracy_score(true_labels_d, conf_preds)\n        trust_accuracy = accuracy_score(true_labels_d, trust_preds)\n        random_accuracy = accuracy_score(true_labels_d, random_preds)\n\n        # Statistical tests\n        _, dir_pvalue = binomial_test_on_directional_rule(disagreements, majority_class)\n\n        # McNemar's tests between directional rule and baselines\n        _, mcnemar_conf_pvalue = mcnemar_test(true_labels_d, dir_preds, conf_preds)\n        _, mcnemar_trust_pvalue = mcnemar_test(true_labels_d, dir_preds, trust_preds)\n        _, mcnemar_random_pvalue = mcnemar_test(true_labels_d, dir_preds, random_preds)\n\n    else:\n        dir_accuracy = conf_accuracy = trust_accuracy = random_accuracy = 0.0\n        dir_pvalue = mcnemar_conf_pvalue = mcnemar_trust_pvalue = mcnemar_random_pvalue = 1.0\n        dir_preds = conf_preds = trust_preds = random_preds = []\n\n    # Overall accuracies\n    simple_accuracy = accuracy_score(test_labels, simple_preds)\n    complex_accuracy = accuracy_score(test_labels, complex_preds)\n\n    result = {\n        'dataset': dataset_name,\n        'sample_size': sample_size,\n        'imbalance_ratio': imbalance_ratio,\n        'seed': seed,\n        'train_size': len(train_texts),\n        'test_size': len(test_texts),\n        'simple_accuracy': float(simple_accuracy),\n        'complex_accuracy': float(complex_accuracy),\n        'num_disagreements': len(disagreements),\n        'disagreement_ratio': len(disagreements) / len(test_texts) if len(test_texts) > 0 else 0,\n        'majority_class': int(majority_class),\n        'class_distribution': dict(Counter(sub_labels)),\n        'directional_rule_accuracy': float(dir_accuracy),\n        'confidence_baseline_accuracy': float(conf_accuracy),\n        'trust_score_baseline_accuracy': float(trust_accuracy),\n        'random_baseline_accuracy': float(random_accuracy),\n        'directional_rule_pvalue': float(dir_pvalue),\n        'mcnemar_vs_confidence_pvalue': float(mcnemar_conf_pvalue),\n        'mcnemar_vs_trust_score_pvalue': float(mcnemar_trust_pvalue),\n        'mcnemar_vs_random_pvalue': float(mcnemar_random_pvalue),\n    }\n\n    logger.info(\n        f\"Completed: size={sample_size}, seed={seed}, \"\n        f\"disagreements={len(disagreements)}, dir_acc={dir_accuracy:.3f}\"\n    )\n\n    return result\n\n\ndef run_all_experiments() -> list[dict[str, Any]]:\n    \"\"\"Run all experiment configurations.\"\"\"\n    logger.info(\"Starting all experiments\")\n\n    # Load datasets\n    sst2_texts, sst2_labels = load_sst2()\n    imdb_texts, imdb_labels = load_imdb()\n\n    dataset_map = {\n        'sst2': (sst2_texts, sst2_labels),\n        'imdb': (imdb_texts, imdb_labels)\n    }\n\n    all_results = []\n\n    # Generate all configurations\n    configs = []\n    for dataset_name in DATASETS:\n        texts, labels = dataset_map[dataset_name]\n        for texts, labels,\n                        sample_size, imbalance_ratio, seed\n                    ))\n\n    logger.info(f\"Total configurations: {len(configs)}\")\n\n    # Run in parallel with ProcessPoolExecutor\n    # Use spawn context to avoid loguru deadlock issues\n    mp_context = mp.get_context(\"spawn\")\n    with ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=NUM_WORKERS, mp_context=mp_context)          config = futures[future]\n            try:\n                result = future.result()\n                all_results.append(result)\n            except Exception as e:\n  all_results.append({\n                    'dataset': dataset_name,\n                    'sample_size': sample_size,\n                    'imbalance_ratio': imbalance_ratio,\n                    'seed': seed,\n                    'error': str(e)\n                })\n\n    logger.info(f\"Completed {len(all_results)} experiments\")\n    return all_results\n\n\n# f\"{dataset}_size{sample_size}_imb{imbalance_ratio}\"\n                summary[key] = {\n                    'dataset': dataset,\n                    'sample_size': sample_size,\n                    'imbalance_ratio': imbalance_ratio,\n                    'n_seeds': len(config_results),\n                    'mean_directional_accuracy': float(np.mean([r['directional_rule_accuracy'] for r in    }\n\n    return summary\n\n\ndef save_results(results: list[dict], ablation: dict):\n    \"\"\"Save results to JSON files.\"\"\"\n    # Main output\n    output = {\n        'metadata': {\n valid\n\n\ndef smoke_test():\n    \"\"\"Run smoke test with one dataset, one seed, size=100.\"\"\"\n    logger.info(\"Running smoke test\")\n\n    try:\n        result = run_single_experiment(\n            dataset_name='sst2',\n            texts=['sample text 1', 'sample text 2'] * 50,  # Dummy data for quick test\n            labels=[0, 1] * 50,\n            sample_size=100,\n            imbalance_ratio=0.5,\n            seed=0\n        )\n\n        assert 'num_disagreements' in result\n        assert 'directional_rule_accuracy' in result\n        assert 'confidence_baseline_accuracy' {mean_trust_acc:.3f}\")\n    print(f\"Mean random baseline accuracy: {mean_rand_acc:.3f}\")\n    print(\"=\"*60 + \"\\n\")\n\n    logger.info(\"Experiment completed successfully\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n", "new_content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Disagreement Direction Test for Sentiment Classification.\n\nCompares TF-IDF Logistic Regression vs character n-gram RandomForest\non small sentiment datasets, analyzing whether disagreement direction\npredicts the correct label better than chance and concrete baselines.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport gc\nimport json\nimport math\nimport multiprocessing as mp\nimport os\nimport resource\nimport sys\nimport time\nfrom collections import Counter\nfrom concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor, as_completed\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Any\n\nimport numpy as np\nfrom datasets import load_dataset\nfrom loguru import logger\nfrom scipy.stats import binomtest\nfrom sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier\nfrom sklearn.feature_extraction.text import CountVectorizer, TfidfVectorizer\nfrom sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression\nfrom sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score\nfrom sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split\nfrom sklearn.neighbors import NearestNeighbors\nfrom sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline\n\n# ============================================================================\n# CONFIGURATION AND CONSTANTS\n# ============================================================================\n\nWORKSPACE = Path(\n    \"/ai-inventor/aii_data/runs/run_q27XJGeAT3TE/3_invention_loop/iter_1/gen_art/gen_art_experiment_1\"\n)\nLOG_DIR = WORKSPACE / \"logs\"\nOUTPUT_DIR = WORKSPACE / \"results\"\nLOG_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)\nOUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)\n\nDATASETS = [\"sst2\", \"imdb\"]\nSAMPLE_SIZES = [100, 200, 500, 1000]\nIMBALANCE_RATIOS = [0.5, 0.7, 0.9]  # majority:minority ratio\nSEEDS = list(range(10))\nNUM_WORKERS = 2  # Container has 2 CPUs\n\n# Memory limits based on container resources (14GB RAM)\nRAM_BUDGET = 12 * 1024**3  # 12GB\n\n# ============================================================================\n# LOGGING SETUP\n# ============================================================================\n\nlogger.remove()\nlogger.add(\n    sys.stdout,\n    level=\"INFO\",\n    format=\"{time:HH:mm:ss}|{level:<7}|{message}\",\n)\nlogger.add(\n    LOG_DIR / \"run.log\",\n    rotation=\"30 MB\",\n    level=\"DEBUG\",\n)\n\n# ============================================================================\n# HARDWARE DETECTION\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef _detect_cpus() -> int:\n    \"\"\"Detect actual CPU allocation (containers/pods/bare metal).\"\"\"\n    try:  # cgroups v2 quota\n        parts = Path(\"/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.max\").read_text().split()\n        if parts[0] != \"max\":\n            return max(1, math.ceil(int(parts[0]) / int(parts[1])))\n    except (FileNotFoundError, ValueError):\n        pass\n    try:  # cgroups v1 quota\n        q = int(Path(\"/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/cpu.cfs_quota_us\").read_text())\n        p = int(Path(\"/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/cpu.cfs_period_us\").read_text())\n        if q > 0:\n            return max(1, math.ceil(q / p))\n    except (FileNotFoundError, ValueError):\n        pass\n    try:  # CPU affinity (cpuset \u2014 used by RunPod, Docker --cpuset-cpus)\n        return len(os.sched_getaffinity(0))\n    except (AttributeError, OSError):\n        pass\n    return os.cpu_count() or 1\n\nNUM_CPUS = _detect_cpus()\nlogger.info(f\"Detected {NUM_CPUS} CPUs\")\n\n# Set memory limits\nresource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_AS, (RAM_BUDGET * 3, RAM_BUDGET * 3))\n\n# ============================================================================\n# MODEL DEFINITIONS\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef get_simple_model():\n    \"\"\"Simple model: TF-IDF + Logistic Regression.\"\"\"\n    return Pipeline([\n        ('tfidf', TfidfVectorizer(max_features=10000, ngram_range=(1, 2))),\n        ('clf', LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000, random_state=42, n_jobs=1))\n    ])\n\n\ndef get_complex_model():\n    \"\"\"Complex model: character n-grams + RandomForest.\"\"\"\n    return Pipeline([\n        ('char_ngram', CountVectorizer(\n            analyzer='char',\n            ngram_range=(3, 5),\n            max_features=20000\n        )),\n        ('clf', RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=100, random_state=42, n_jobs=1))\n    ])\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# DATA LOADING AND PREPARATION\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef load_sst2():\n    \"\"\"Load SST-2 dataset.\"\"\"\n    logger.info(\"Loading SST-2 dataset\")\n    ds = load_dataset(\"stanfordnlp/sst2\", split=\"train\")\n    texts = ds[\"sentence\"]\n    labels = ds[\"label\"]\n    del ds\n    gc.collect()\n    return texts, labels\n\n\ndef load_imdb():\n    \"\"\"Load IMDB dataset.\"\"\"\n    logger.info(\"Loading IMDB dataset\")\n    ds = load_dataset(\"stanfordnlp/imdb\", split=\"train\")\n    texts = ds[\"text\"]\n    labels = ds[\"label\"]\n    del ds\n    gc.collect()\n    return texts, labels\n\n\ndef stratified_imbalanced_subsample(\n    texts: list[str],\n    labels: list[int],\n    target_size: int,\n    imbalance_ratio: float,\n    random_state: int\n) -> tuple[list[str], list[int]]:\n    \"\"\"Create a stratified subsample with controlled class imbalance.\n\n    Args:\n        texts: List of text samples\n        labels: List of labels\n        target_size: Total target sample size\n        imbalance_ratio: Ratio of majority to minority class (0.5 = balanced)\n        random_state: Random seed\n\n    Returns:\n        Subsampled texts and labels\n    \"\"\"\n    rng = np.random.RandomState(random_state)\n\n    # Separate by class\n    class_0_idx = [i for i, l in enumerate(labels) if l == 0]\n    class_1_idx = [i for i, l in enumerate(labels) if l == 1]\n\n    # Calculate sizes based on imbalance ratio\n    # imbalance_ratio = majority_size / minority_size\n    # total = majority_size + minority_size\n    minority_size = int(target_size / (1 + imbalance_ratio))\n    majority_size = target_size - minority_size\n\n    # Sample from each class\n    sampled_0 = rng.choice(class_0_idx, size=min(majority_size, len(class_0_idx)), replace=False)\n    sampled_1 = rng.choice(class_1_idx, size=min(minority_size, len(class_1_idx)), replace=False)\n\n    # Combine and shuffle\n    indices = np.concatenate([sampled_0, sampled_1])\n    rng.shuffle(indices)\n\n    return [texts[i] for i in indices], [labels[i] for i in indices]\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# BASELINE METHODS\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef confidence_baseline(disagreements: list[dict]) -> list[int]:\n    \"\"\"Baseline: predict whichever model has higher confidence.\"\"\"\n    predictions = []\n    for d in disagreements:\n        if d['prob_simple'] > d['prob_complex']:\n            predictions.append(d['pred_simple'])\n        else:\n            predictions.append(d['pred_complex'])\n    return predictions\n\n\ndef trust_score_baseline(disagreements: list[dict], train_texts: list[str], train_labels: list[int]) -> list[int]:\n    \"\"\"Baseline: trust-score style proxy using nearest-neighbor agreement.\"\"\"\n    # Build TF-IDF representation of training data\n    vectorizer = TfidfVectorizer(max_features=10000, ngram_range=(1, 2))\n    try:\n        train_tfidf = vectorizer.fit_transform(train_texts)\n        nn = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=5, metric='cosine')\n        nn.fit(train_tfidf)\n\n        predictions = []\n        for d in disagreements:\n            # Transform test text\n            test_vec = vectorizer.transform([d['text']])\n            distances, indices = \"\"\"Create a stratified subsample with controlled class imbalance.\n\n    Args:\n        texts: List of text samples\n        labels: List of labels\n        target_size: Total target sample size\n        imbalance_ratio: Ratio of majority to minority class (0.5 = balanced)\n        random_state: Random seed\n\n    Returns:\n        Subsampled texts and labels\n    \"\"\"\n    rng = np.random.RandomState(random_state)\n\n    # Separate by class\n    class_0_idx = [i for i, l in enumerate(labels) if l == 0]\n    class_1_idx = [i for i, l in enumerate(labels) if l == 1]\n\n    # Calculate sizes based on imbalance ratio\n    # imbalance_ratio = majority_size / minority_size\n    # total = majority_size + minority_size\n    minority_size = int(target_size / (1 + imbalance_ratio))\n    majority_size = target_size - minority_size\n\n    # Sample from each class\n    sampled_0 = rng.choice(class_0_idx, size=min(majority_size, len(class_0_idx)), replace=False)\n    sampled_1 = rng.choice(class_1_idx, size=min(minority_size, len(class_1_idx)), replace=False)\n\n    # Combine and shuffle\n    indices = np.concatenate([sampled_0, sampled_1])\n    rng.shuffle(indices)\n\n    return [texts[i] for i in indices], [labels[i] for i in indices]\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# BASELINE METHODS\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef confidence_baseline(disagreements: list[dict]) -> list[int]:\n    \"\"\"Baseline: predict whichever model has higher confidence.\"\"\"\n    predictions = []\n    for d in disagreements:\n        if d['prob_simple'] > d['prob_complex']:\n            predictions.append(d['pred_simple'])\n        else:\n            predictions.append(d['pred_complex'])\n    return predictions\n\n\ndef trust_score_baseline(disagreements: list[dict], train_texts: list[str], train_labels: list[int]) -> list[int]:\n    \"\"\"Baseline: trust-score style proxy using nearest-neighbor agreement.\"\"\"\n    # Build TF-IDF representation of training data\n    vectorizer = TfidfVectorizer(max_features=10000, ngram_range=(1, 2))\n    try:\n        train_tfidf = vectorizer.fit_transform(train_texts)\n        nn = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=5, metric='cosine')\n        nn.fit(train_tfidf)\n\n        predictions = []\n        for d in disagreements:\n            # Transform test text\n            test_vec = vectorizer.transform([d['text']])\n            distances, indices = nn.kneighbors(test_vec)\n            neighbor_labels = [train_labels[i] for i in indices[0]]\n            majority_label = Counter(neighbor_labels).most_common(1)[0][0]\n            predictions.append(majority_label)\n    except Exception as e:\n        logger.warning(f\"Trust score baseline failed: {e}\")\n        # Fallback to random\n        predictions = [np.random.choice([0, 1]) for _ in disagreements]\n\n    return predictions\n\n\ndef random_baseline(n: int) -> list[int]:\n    \"\"\"Random baseline.\"\"\"\n    return np.random.RandomState(42).randint(0, 2, size=n).tolist()\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# STATISTICAL TESTS\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef binomial_test_on_directional_rule(disagreements: list[dict], majority_class: int) -> tuple[float, float]:\n    \"\"\"Test if directional rule accuracy > 50% using binomial test.\"\"\"\n    correct = sum(\n        1 for d in disagreements\n        if (d['pred_simple'] == majority_class and d['pred_simple'] == d['true_label']) or\n           (d['pred_simple'] != majority_class and d['pred_complex'] == d['true_label'])\n    )\n    n = len(disagreements)\n    if n == 0:\n        return 0.0, 1.0\n    result = binomtest(correct, n, 0.5, alternative='greater')\n    p_value = result.pvalue\n    accuracy = correct / n\n    return accuracy, p_value\n\n\ndef mcnemar_test(y_true: list[int], pred1: list[int], pred2: list[int]) -> tuple[float, float]:\n    \"\"\"McNemar's test between two prediction sets.\"\"\"\n    # Contingency table\n    a = sum(1 for yt, p1, p2 in zip(y_true, pred1, pred2)\n            if p1 == yt and p2 != yt)  # pred1 correct, pred2 wrong\n    b = sum(1 for yt, p1, p2 in zip(y_true, pred1, pred2)\n            if p1 != yt and p2 == yt)  # pred1 wrong, pred2 correct\n    c = sum(1 for yt, p1, p2 in zip(y_true, pred1, pred2)\n            if p1 != yt and p2 != yt)  # both wrong\n    d = sum(1 for yt, p1, p2 in zip(y_true, pred1, pred2)\n            if p1 == yt and p2 == yt)  # both correct\n\n    # McNemar's test on discordant pairs\n    if a + b == 0:\n        return 0.0, 1.0\n\n    # Use binomial approximation for McNemar's test\n    # For larger samples, chi-square with continuity correction\n    if a + b < 25:\n        result = binomtest(a, a + b, 0.5, alternative='two-sided')\n        p_value = result.pvalue\n    else:\n        chi2 = (abs(a - b) - 1) ** 2 / (a + b)\n        p_value = stats.chi2.sf(chi2, 1)\n\n    accuracy1 = (a + d) / len(y_true) if len(y_true) > 0 else 0\n    accuracy2 = (b + d) / len(y_true) if len(y_true) > 0 else 0\n\n    return accuracy1, p_value\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# EXPERIMENT EXECUTION\n# true_labels_d = [d['true_label'] for d in disagreements]\n\n        # Compute metrics\n        dir_accuracy = accuracy_score(true_labels_d, dir_preds)\n        conf_accuracy = \"__main__\":\n    main()\n", "new_content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Disagreement Direction Test for Sentiment Classification.\n\nCompares TF-IDF Logistic Regression vs character n-gram
