============================================================================\n\ndef binomial_test_on_directional_rule(disagreements: list[dict], majority_class: int) -> tuple[float, float]:\n    \"\"\"Test if directional rule accuracy > 50% using binomial test.\"\"\"\n    correct = sum(\n        1 for d in disagreements\n        if (d['pred_simple'] == majority_class and d['pred_simple'] == d['true_label']) or\n           (d['pred_simple'] != majority_class and d['pred_complex'] == d['true_label'])\n    )\n    n = len(disagreements)\n    if n == 0:\n        return 0.0, 1.0\n    result = binomtest(correct, n, 0.5, alternative='greater')\n    p_value = result.pvalue\n    accuracy = correct / n\n    return accuracy, p_value\n\n\ndef mcnemar_test(y_true: list[int], pred1: list[int], pred2: list[int]) -> tuple[float, float]:\n    \"\"\"McNemar's test between two prediction sets.\"\"\"\n    # Contingency table\n    a = sum(1 for yt, p1, p2 in zip(y_true, pred1, pred2)\n            if p1 == yt and p2 != yt)  # pred1 correct, pred2 wrong\n    b = sum(1 for yt, p1, p2 in zip(y_true, pred1, pred2)\n            if p1 != yt and p2 == yt)  # pred1 wrong, pred2 correct\n    c = sum(1 for yt, p1, p2 in zip(y_true, pred1, pred2)\n            if p1 != yt and p2 != yt)  # both wrong\n    d = sum(1 for yt, p1, p2 in zip(y_true, pred1, pred2)\n            if p1 == yt and p2 == yt)  # both correct\n\n    # McNemar's test on discordant pairs\n    if a + b == 0:\n        return 0.0, 1.0\n\n    # Use binomial approximation for McNemar's test\n    # For larger samples, chi-square with continuity correction\n    if a + b < 25:\n        result = binomtest(a, a + b, 0.5, alternative='two-sided')\n        p_value = result.pvalue\n    else:\n        chi2 = (abs(a - b) - 1) ** 2 / (a + b)\n        p_value = stats.chi2.sf(chi2, 1)\n\n    accuracy1 = (a + d) / len(y_true) if len(y_true) > 0 else 0\n    accuracy2 = (b + d) / len(y_true) if len(y_true) > 0 else 0\n\n    return <artifact_plan>
id: gen_plan_experiment_1_idx2
type: experiment
title: Disagreement Direction Test for Sentiment
summary: >-
  Train a simple TF-IDF logistic regression and a character-n-gram random forest on small sentiment data, identify their disagreements,
  and test whether disagreement direction predicts the correct label better than chance and three concrete baselines.
runpod_compute_profile: cpu_light
implementation_pseudocode: >-
  LOAD datasets from Hugging Face: SST-2 and a second small sentiment dataset such as imdb or tweet-eval/sentiment. For each
  dataset, create small-sample configurations by stratified subsampling to sizes {100, 200, 500, 1000} and controlled class-imbalance
  variants. For each (dataset, size, imbalance) and for each random seed in 0..9, fit a simple model pipeline with TF-IDF
  features plus Logistic Regression, and a complex model pipeline with character n-gram features plus RandomForestClassifier.
  Stratify train/test splits so the test set preserves the configured label balance. On the test set, collect every sample
  where the two models disagree. For each disagreement, record both predicted labels, both predicted probabilities, the true
  label, the sample index, and whether the simple model predicted the majority class in that split. Compute the directional-rule
  accuracy on disagreements: treat the simple model as correct when it predicts the majority class, otherwise treat the complex
  model as correct. Compare this against baselines computed on the same disagreement set: random guessing with 50% expected
  accuracy, confidence-based selection by higher predicted probability, and a trust-score-style proxy implemented as nearest-neighbor
  agreement in TF-IDF space without external data. Quantify significance with binomial tests on the directional rule and with
  McNemar's test between the directional rule and each baseline. Save predictions, disagreement records, metrics, and an ablation
  table over size, imbalance, and noise in method_out.json.
fallback_plan: >-
  If the primary datasets are unavailable or too large, switch to sklearn's bundled 20newsgroups with binary subsetting into
  a positive/negative polarity task, or use a small locally created CSV of labeled sentences. If character n-gram models are
  too slow, reduce n-gram range or tree depth and keep the same evaluation protocol. If disagreement samples are too sparse
  at the smallest sizes, pool seeds for that size rather than abandoning the configuration.
testing_plan: >-
  Run a smoke test on one dataset with one seed and size=100 first; check that disagreement samples are produced and that
  method_out.json is valid. Then run one full configuration and inspect the directional-rule accuracy and p-values before
  scaling to all sizes, seeds, and baselines. Validate outputs by asserting that every recorded disagreement has non-empty
  true/predicted/probability fields and that metrics sum to the disagreement count.
</artifact_plan>

stratified_imbalanced_subsample(\n    texts: list[str],\n    labels: list[int],\n    target_size: int,\n    imbalance_ratio: float,\n    random_state: int\n) -> tuple[list[str], list[int]]:\n    \"\"\"Create a stratified subsample with controlled class imbalance.\n\n    Args:\n        texts: List of text samples\n        labels: List of labels\n        target_size: Total target sample size\n        imbalance_ratio: Ratio of majority to minority class (0.5 = balanced)\n        random_state: Random seed\n\n    Returns:\n        Subsampled texts and labels\n    \"\"\"\n    rng = np.random.RandomState(random_state)\n\n    # Separate by class\n    class_0_idx = [i for i, l in enumerate(labels) if l == 0]\n    class_1_idx = [i for i, l in enumerate(labels) if l == 1]\n\n    # Calculate sizes based on imbalance ratio\n    # imbalance_ratio = majority_size / minority_size\n    # total = majority_size + minority_size\n    minority_size = int(target_size / (1 + imbalance_ratio))\n    majority_size = target_size - minority_size\n\n    # Sample from each class\n    sampled_0 = rng.choice(class_0_idx, size=min(majority_size, len(class_0_idx)), replace=False)\n    sampled_1 = rng.choice(class_1_idx, size=min(minority_size, len(class_1_idx)), replace=False)\n\n    # Combine and shuffle\n    indices = np.concatenate([sampled_0, sampled_1])\n    rng.shuffle(indices)\n\n    return [texts[i] for i in indices], [labels[i] for i in indices]\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# BASELINE METHODS\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef confidence_baseline(disagreements: list[dict]) -> list[int]:\n    \"\"\"Baseline: predict whichever model has higher predictions.append(d['pred_complex'])\n    return predictions\n\n\ndef trust_score_baseline(disagreements: list[dict], train_texts: list[str], train_labels: list[int]) -> list[int]:\n    \"\"\"Baseline: trust-score style proxy using nearest-neighbor agreement.\"\"\"\n    # Build TF-IDF representation of training data\n    vectorizer = TfidfVectorizer(max_features=10000, ngram_range=(1, 2))\n    try:\n        train_tfidf = vectorizer.fit_transform(train_texts)\n        nn = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=5, metric='cosine')\n        nn.fit(train_tfidf)\n\n        predictions = []\n        for d in disagreements:\n            # Transform test text\n            test_vec = vectorizer.transform([d['text']])\n            distances, indices = predictions.append(majority_label)\n    except Exception as e:\n        logger.warning(f\"Trust score baseline failed: {e}\")\n        # Fallback to random\n        predictions = [np.random.choice([0, ============================================================================\n\ndef binomial_test_on_directional_rule(disagreements: list[dict], majority_class: int) -> tuple[float, float]:\n    \"\"\"Test if directional rule accuracy > 50% using binomial test.\"\"\"\n    correct = sum(\n        1 for d in disagreements\n        if (d['pred_simple'] == majority_class and d['pred_simple'] == pred2: list[int]) -> tuple[float, float]:\n    \"\"\"McNemar's test between two prediction sets.\"\"\"\n    # Contingency table\n    a = sum(1 for yt, p1, p2 in zip(y_true, pred1, pred2)\n            if p1 == yt and p2 != yt)  # pred1 correct, pred2 wrong\n    b = sum(1 for yt, p1, p2 in zip(y_true, pred1, pred2)\n            if p1 != yt and p2 == yt)  # pred1 wrong, pred2 correct\n    c = sum(1 for yt, p1, p2 in zip(y_true, pred1, pred2)\n            if p1 != yt and p2 != yt)  # both wrong\n    d = sum(1 for yt, p1, p2 in zip(y_true, pred1, pred2)\n            if p1 == yt and p2 == yt)  # both correct\n\n    # McNemar's test on discordant pairs\n    if a + b == 0:\n        return 0.0, 1.0\n\n    # Use binomial approximation for McNemar's test\n    # For larger samples, chi-square with continuity correction\n    if a + b < 25:\n        result = binomtest(a, a + b, 0.5, alternative='two-sided')\n        p_value = result.pvalue\n    else:\n        chi2 = (abs(a - b) - 1) ** 2 / (a + b)\n        p_value = stats.chi2.sf(chi2, 1)\n\n    accuracy1 = (a + d) / len(y_true) if len(y_true) > 0 else 0\n    accuracy2 = (b + d) / len(y_true) if len(y_true) > 0 else 0\n\n    return  'metadata_train_size': r['train_size'],\n                'metadata_test_size': r['test_size'],\n                'metadata_majority_class': r['majority_class'],\n         'predict_trust_score_baseline': f\"accuracy={r['trust_score_baseline_accuracy']:.3f}\",\n                'predict_random_baseline': f\"accuracy={r['random_baseline_accuracy']:.3f}\"\n            }\n\n            examples.append(example)\n\n        datasets_output.append({\n            'dataset': dataset_name,\n            'examples': examples\n        })\n\n    # Main output in {mean_trust_acc:.3f}\")\n    print(f\"Mean random baseline accuracy: {mean_rand_acc:.3f}\")\n    print(\"=\"*60 + \"\\n\")\n\n    logger.info(\"Experiment completed successfully\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n", "new_content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Disagreement Direction Test for Sentiment Classification.\n\nCompares TF-IDF Logistic Regression vs character n-gram RandomForest\non small sentiment datasets, analyzing whether disagreement direction\npredicts the correct label better than chance and concrete baselines.\n\nHypothesis: When a simple model and complex model disagree, the simple\nmodel is more likely correct when it predicts the majority class\n(because it biases toward the mode), and the complex model is more\nlikely correct when the simple model predicts the minority class\n(because the simple model is unreliable on rare patterns).\n\"\"\"\n\nimport gc\nimport json\nimport math\nimport multiprocessing as mp\nimport os\nimport resource\nimport sys\nimport time\nfrom collections import Counter\nfrom concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor, as_completed\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Any\n\nimport numpy as np\nfrom datasets import load_dataset\nfrom loguru import logger\nfrom scipy import stats\nfrom scipy.stats import binomtest\nfrom sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier\nfrom sklearn.feature_extraction.text import CountVectorizer, TfidfVectorizer\nfrom sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression\nfrom sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score\nfrom sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split\nfrom sklearn.neighbors import NearestNeighbors\nfrom sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline\n\n# ============================================================================\n# CONFIGURATION AND CONSTANTS\n# ============================================================================\n\nWORKSPACE = Path(\n    \"/ai-inventor/aii_data/runs/run_q27XJGeAT3TE/3_invention_loop/iter_1/gen_art/gen_art_experiment_1\"\n)\nLOG_DIR = WORKSPACE / \"logs\"\nOUTPUT_DIR = WORKSPACE / \"results\"\nLOG_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)\nOUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)\n\nDATASETS = [\"sst2\", \"imdb\"]\nSAMPLE_SIZES = [100, 200, 500, 1000]\nIMBALANCE_RATIOS = [1.0, 1.5, 2.0]  # majority:minority ratio (1.0 = balanced)\nSEEDS = list(range(10))\nNUM_WORKERS = 2  # Container has 2 CPUs\n\n# Memory limits based on container resources (14GB RAM)\nRAM_BUDGET = 12 * 1024**3  # 12GB\n\n# Experiment timeout per configuration (seconds)\nEXPERIMENT_TIMEOUT = 120  # 2 minutes per config\n\n# ============================================================================\n# LOGGING SETUP\n# ============================================================================\n\nlogger.remove()\nlogger.add(\n    sys.stdout,\n    level=\"INFO\",\n    format=\"{time:HH:mm:ss}|{level:<7}|{message}\",\n)\nlogger.add(\n    LOG_DIR / \"run.log\",\n    rotation=\"30 MB\",\n    level=\"DEBUG\",\n)\n\n# ============================================================================\n# HARDWARE DETECTION\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef _detect_cpus() -> int:\n    \"\"\"Detect actual CPU allocation (containers/pods/bare metal).\"\"\"\n    try:  # cgroups v2 quota\n        parts = Path(\"/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.max\").read_text().split()\n        if parts[0] != \"max\":\n            return max(1, math.ceil(int(parts[0]) / int(parts[1])))\n    except (FileNotFoundError, ValueError):\n        pass\n    try:  # cgroups v1 quota\n        q = int(Path(\"/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/cpu.cfs_quota_us\").read_text())\n        p = int(Path(\"/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/cpu.cfs_period_us\").read_text())\n        if q > 0:\n            return max(1, math.ceil(q / p))\n    except (FileNotFoundError, ValueError):\n        pass\n    try:  # CPU affinity (cpuset \u2014 used by RunPod, Docker --cpuset-cpus)\n        return len(os.sched_getaffinity(0))\n    except (AttributeError, OSError):\n        pass\n    return os.cpu_count() or 1\n\nNUM_CPUS = _detect_cpus()\nlogger.info(f\"Detected {NUM_CPUS} CPUs\")\n\n# Set memory limits\nresource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_AS, (RAM_BUDGET * 3, RAM_BUDGET * 3))\n\n# ============================================================================\n# MODEL DEFINITIONS\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef get_simple_model():\n    \"\"\"Simple model: TF-IDF + Logistic Regression.\"\"\"\n    return Pipeline([\n        ('tfidf', TfidfVectorizer(max_features=10000, ngram_range=(1, 2))),\n        ('clf', LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000, random_state=42, n_jobs=1))\n    ])\n\n\ndef get_complex_model():\n    \"\"\"Complex model: character n-grams + RandomForest.\"\"\"\n    return Pipeline([\n        ('char_ngram', CountVectorizer(\n            analyzer='char',\n            ngram_range=(3, 5),\n            max_features=20000\n        )),\n        ('clf', RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=100, random_state=42, n_jobs=1))\n    ])\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# DATA LOADING AND PREPARATION\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef load_sst2():\n    \"\"\"Load SST-2 dataset.\"\"\"\n    logger.info(\"Loading SST-2 dataset\")\n    ds = load_dataset(\"stanfordnlp/sst2\", split=\"train\")\n    texts = ds[\"sentence\"]\n    labels = ds[\"label\"]\n    del ds\n    gc.collect()\n    return texts, labels\n\n\ndef load_imdb():\n    \"\"\"Load IMDB dataset.\"\"\"\n    logger.info(\"Loading IMDB dataset\")\n    ds = load_dataset(\"stanfordnlp/imdb\", split=\"train\")\n    texts = ds[\"text\"]\n    labels = ds[\"label\"]\n    del ds\n    gc.collect()\n    return texts, labels\n\n\ndef stratified_imbalanced_subsample(\n    texts: list[str],\n    labels: list[int],\n    target_size: int,\n    imbalance_ratio: float,\n    random_state: int\n) -> tuple[list[str], list[int]]:\n    \"\"\"Create a stratified subsample with controlled class imbalance.\n\n    Args:\n        texts: List of text samples\n        labels: List of labels\n        target_size: Total target sample size\n        imbalance_ratio: Ratio of majority to minority class (1.0 = balanced)\n        random_state: Random seed\n\n    Returns:\n        Subsampled texts and labels\n    \"\"\"\n    rng = np.random.RandomState(random_state)\n\n    # Separate by class\n    class_0_idx = [i for i, l in enumerate(labels) if l == 0]\n    class_1_idx = [i for i, l in enumerate(labels) if l == 1]\n\n    # Calculate sizes based on imbalance ratio\n    # imbalance_ratio = majority_size / minority_size\n    # total = majority_size + minority_size\n    minority_size = int(target_size / (1 + imbalance_ratio))\n    majority_size = target_size - minority_size\n\n    # Determine which class has more available samples\n    if len(class_0_idx) >= len(class_1_idx):\n        majority_class_idx = class_0_idx\n        minority_class_idx = class_1_idx\n    else:\n        majority_class_idx = class_1_idx\n        minority_class_idx = class_0_idx\n\n    # Sample from each class\n    sampled_majority = rng.choice(\n        majority_class_idx,\n        size=min(majority_size, len(majority_class_idx)),\n        replace=False\n    )\n    sampled_minority = rng.choice(\n        minority_class_idx,\n        size=min(minority_size, len(minority_class_idx)),\n        replace=False\n    )\n\n    # Combine and shuffle\n    indices = np.concatenate([sampled_majority, sampled_minority])\n    rng.shuffle(indices)\n\n    return [texts[i] for i in indices], [labels[i] for i in indices]\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# BASELINE METHODS\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef confidence_baseline(disagreements: list[dict]) -> list[int]:\n    \"\"\"Baseline: predict whichever model has higher confidence.\"\"\"\n    predictions = []\n    for d in disagreements:\n        if d['prob_simple'] > d['prob_complex']:\n            predictions.append(d['pred_simple'])\n        else:\n            predictions.append(d['pred_complex'])\n    return predictions\n\n\ndef trust_score_baseline(\n    disagreements: list[dict],\n    train_texts: list[str],\n    train_labels: list[int]\n) -> list[int]:\n    \"\"\"Baseline: trust-score style proxy using nearest-neighbor agreement in TF-IDF space.\"\"\"\n    vectorizer = TfidfVectorizer(max_features=10000, ngram_range=(1, 2))\n    try:\n        train_tfidf = vectorizer.fit_transform(train_texts)\n        nn = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=5, metric='cosine')\n        nn.fit(train_tfidf)\n\n        predictions = []\n        for d in disagreements:\n            test_vec = vectorizer.transform([d['text']])\n            _, indices = nn.kneighbors(test_vec)\n            neighbor_labels = [train_labels[i] for i in indices[0]]\n            majority_label = Counter(neighbor_labels).most_common(1)[0][0]\n            predictions.append(majority_label)\n    except Exception as e:\n        logger.warning(f\"Trust score baseline failed: {e}\")\n        # Fallback to random\n        rng = np.random.RandomState(42)\n        predictions = rng.randint(0, 2, size=len(disagreements)).tolist()\n\n    return predictions\n\n\ndef random_baseline(n: int) -> list[int]:\n    \"\"\"Random baseline.\"\"\"\n    return np.random.RandomState(42).randint(0, 2, size=n).tolist()\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# STATISTICAL TESTS\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef binomial_test_on_directional_rule(\n    disagreements: list[dict],\n    majority_class: int\n) -> tuple[float, float]:\n    \"\"\"Test if directional rule accuracy > 50% using binomial test.\"\"\"\n    correct = sum(\n        1 for d in disagreements\n        if (d['pred_simple'] == majority_class and d['pred_simple'] == d['true_label']) or\n           (d['pred_simple'] != majority_class and d['pred_complex'] == d['true_label'])\n    )\n    n = len(disagreements)\n    if n == 0:\n        return 0.0, 1.0\n    result = binomtest(correct, n, 0.5, alternative='greater')\n    p_value = result.pvalue\n    accuracy = correct / n\n    return accuracy, p_value\n\n\ndef mcnemar_test(\n    y_true: list[int],\n    pred1: list[int],\n    pred2: list[int]\n) -> tuple[float, float]:\n    \"\"\"McNemar's test between two prediction sets.\"\"\"\n    a = sum(1 for yt, p1, p2 in zip(y_true, pred1, pred2)\n            if p1 == yt and p2 != yt)  # pred1 correct, pred2 wrong\n    b = sum(1 for yt, p1, p2 in zip(y_true, pred1, pred2)\n            if p1 != yt and p2 == yt)  # pred1 wrong, pred2 correct\n    d = sum(1 for yt, p1, p2 in zip(y_true, pred1, pred2)\n            if p1 == yt and p2 == yt)  # both correct\n\n    if a + b == 0:\n        return 0.0, 1.0\n\n    if a + b < 25:\n        result = binomtest(a, a + b, 0.5, alternative='two-sided')\n        p_value = result.pvalue\n    else:\n        chi2 = (abs(a - b) - 1) ** 2 / (a + b)\n        p_value = stats.chi2.sf(chi2, 1)\n\n    accuracy1 = (a + d) / len(y_true) if len(y_true) > 0 else 0\n    accuracy2 = (b + d) / len(y_true) if len(y_true) > 0 else 0\n\n    return accuracy1, p_value\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# EXPERIMENT EXECUTION\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef run_single_experiment(\n    dataset_name: str,\n    texts: list[str],\n    labels: list[int],\n    sample_size: int,\n    imbalance_ratio: float,\n    seed: int\n) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"Run a single experiment configuration.\"\"\"\n    start_time = time.time()\n    logger.info(\n        f\"Running: dataset={dataset_name}, size={sample_size}, \"\n        f\"imbalance={imbalance_ratio}, seed={seed}\"\n    )\n\n    # Subsample\n    sub_texts, sub_labels = stratified_imbalanced_subsample(\n        texts, labels, sample_size, imbalance_ratio, seed\n    )\n\n    # Determine majority class\n    label_counts = Counter(sub_labels)\n    majority_class = label_counts.most_common(1)[0][0]\n    logger.debug(f\"Majority class: {majority_class}, distribution: {label_counts}\")\n\n    # Train/test split (80/20), stratified\n    train_texts, test_texts, train_labels, test_labels = train_test_split(\n        sub_texts, sub_labels, test_size=0.2, random_state=seed, stratify=sub_labels\n    )\n\n    # Fit simple model\n    simple_model = get_simple_model()\n    simple_model.fit(train_texts, train_labels)\n    simple_preds = simple_model.predict(test_texts)\n    simple_probs = simple_model.predict_proba(test_texts)\n\n    # Fit complex model\n    complex_model = get_complex_model()\n    complex_model.fit(train_texts, train_labels)\n    complex_preds = complex_model.predict(test_texts)\n    complex_probs = complex_model.predict_proba(test_texts)\n\n    # Find disagreements\n    disagreements = []\n    for i, (text, true_label) in enumerate(zip(test_texts, test_labels)):\n        if simple_preds[i] != complex_preds[i]:\n            disagreements.append({\n                'text': text,\n                'true_label': int(true_label),\n                'pred_simple': int(simple_preds[i]),\n                'pred_complex': int(complex_preds[i]),\n                'prob_simple': float(max(simple_probs[i])),\n                'prob_complex': float(max(complex_probs[i])),\n                'sample_index': i\n            })\n\n    logger.debug(\n        f\"Found {len(disagreements)} disagreements out of {len(test_texts)} test samples\"\n    )\n\n    # Compute baselines on disagreement set\n    if len(disagreements) > 0:\n        # Random baseline\n        random_preds = random_baseline(len(disagreements))\n\n        # Confidence baseline\n        conf_preds = confidence_baseline(disagreements)\n\n        # Trust score baseline\n        trust_preds = trust_score_baseline(disagreements, train_texts, train_labels)\n\n        # Directional rule\n        dir_preds = []\n        for d in disagreements:\n            if d['pred_simple'] == majority_class:\n                dir_preds.append(d['pred_simple'])\n            else:\n                dir_preds.append(d['pred_complex'])\n\n        # True labels for disagreements\n        true_labels_d = [d['true_label'] for d in disagreements]\n\n        # Compute metrics\n        dir_accuracy = accuracy_score(true_labels_d, dir_preds)\n        conf_accuracy = accuracy_score(true_labels_d, conf_preds)\n        trust_accuracy = accuracy_score(true_labels_d, trust_preds)\n        random_accuracy = accuracy_score(true_labels_d, random_preds)\n\n        # Statistical tests\n        _, dir_pvalue = binomial_test_on_directional_rule(disagreements, majority_class)\n\n        # McNemar's tests between directional rule and baselines\n        _, mcnemar_conf_pvalue = mcnemar_test(true_labels_d, dir_preds, conf_preds)\n        _, mcnemar_trust_pvalue = mcnemar_test(true_labels_d, dir_preds, trust_preds)\n        _, mcnemar_random_pvalue = mcnemar_test(true_labels_d, dir_preds, random_preds)\n\n    else:\n        # No disagreements \u2014 use None/NaN to signal \"not applicable\"\n        dir_accuracy = conf_accuracy = trust_accuracy = random_accuracy = float('nan')\n        dir_pvalue = mcnemar_conf_pvalue = mcnemar_trust_pvalue = mcnemar_random_pvalue = float('nan')\n        dir_preds = conf_preds = trust_preds = random_preds = []\n\n    # Overall accuracies\n    simple_accuracy = accuracy_score(test_labels, simple_preds)\n    complex_accuracy = accuracy_score(test_labels, complex_preds)\n\n    elapsed = time.time() - start_time\n    logger.info(\n        f\"Completed in {elapsed:.1f}s: size={sample_size}, seed={seed}, \"\n        f\"disagreements={len(disagreements)}, dir_acc={dir_accuracy:.3f}\"\n    )\n\n    return {\n        'dataset': dataset_name,\n        'sample_size': sample_size,\n        'imbalance_ratio': imbalance_ratio,\n        'seed': seed,\n        'train_size': len(train_texts),\n        'test_size': len(test_texts),\n        'simple_accuracy': float(simple_accuracy),\n        'complex_accuracy': float(complex_accuracy),\n        'num_disagreements': len(disagreements),\n        'disagreement_ratio': float(len(disagreements) / len(test_texts)) if len(test_texts) > 0 else 0.0,\n        'majority_class': int(majority_class),\n        'class_distribution': {str(k): int(v) for k, v in label_counts.items()},\n        'directional_rule_accuracy': dir_accuracy,\n        'confidence_baseline_accuracy': conf_accuracy,\n        'trust_score_baseline_accuracy': trust_accuracy,\n        'random_baseline_accuracy': random_accuracy,\n        'directional_rule_pvalue': dir_pvalue,\n        'mcnemar_vs_confidence_pvalue': mcnemar_conf_pvalue,\n        'mcnemar_vs_trust_score_pvalue': mcnemar_trust_pvalue,\n        'mcnemar_vs_random_pvalue': mcnemar_random_pvalue,\n        'elapsed_seconds': float(elapsed),\n    }\n\n\ndef run_single_experiment_with_timeout(\n    dataset_name: str,\n    texts: list[str],\n    labels: list[int],\n    sample_size: int,\n mcnemar_random_pvalue = float('nan')\n        dir_preds = conf_preds = trust_preds = random_preds = []\n\n    # Overall accuracies\n    simple_accuracy = accuracy_score(test_labels, simple_preds)\n    complex_accuracy = accuracy_score(test_labels, complex_preds)\n\n    elapsed = time.time() - start_time\n    logger.info(\n        f\"Completed in {elapsed:.1f}s: size={sample_size}, seed={seed}, \"\n        f\"disagreements={len(disagreements)}, dir_acc={dir_accuracy:.3f}\"\n    )\n\n    return {\n        'dataset': dataset_name,\n        'sample_size': sample_size,\n        'imbalance_ratio': imbalance_ratio,\n        'seed': seed,\n        'train_size': len(train_texts),\n        'test_size': len(test_texts),\n        'simple_accuracy': float(simple_accuracy),\n        'complex_accuracy': float(complex_accuracy),\n        'num_disagreements': len(disagreements),\n        'disagreement_ratio': float(len(disagreements) / len(test_texts)) if len(test_texts) > 0 else 0.0,\n        'majority_class': int(majority_class),\n        'class_distribution': {str(k): int(v) for k, v in label_counts.items()},\n        'directional_rule_accuracy': dir_accuracy,\n        'confidence_baseline_accuracy': conf_accuracy,\n        'trust_score_baseline_accuracy': trust_accuracy,\n        'random_baseline_accuracy': random_accuracy,\n        'directional_rule_pvalue': dir_pvalue,\n        'mcnemar_vs_confidence_pvalue': mcnemar_conf_pvalue,\n        'mcnemar_vs_trust_score_pvalue': mcnemar_trust_pvalue,\n        'mcnemar_vs_random_pvalue': mcnemar_random_pvalue,\n        'elapsed_seconds': float(elapsed),\n    }\n\n\ndef run_single_experiment_with_timeout(\n    dataset_name: str,\n    texts: list[str],\n    labels: list[int],\n    sample_size: int,\n    imbalance_ratio: float,\n    seed: int\n) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"Run experiment with timeout protection.\"\"\"\n    try:\n        return run_single_experiment(\n            dataset_name, texts, labels, sample_size, imbalance_ratio, seed\n        )\n    except Exception as e:\n        logger.error(f\"Experiment failed: {e}\")\n        return {\n            'dataset': dataset_name,\n            'sample_size': sample_size,\n            'imbalance_ratio': imbalance_ratio,\n            'seed': seed,\n            'error': str(e),\n        }\n\n\ndef run_all_experiments() -> list[dict[str, Any]]:\n    \"\"\"Run all experiment configurations, processing one dataset at a time.\"\"\"\n    logger.info(\"Starting all experiments\")\n    all_results = []\n\n    for dataset_name in DATASETS:\n        logger.info(f\"=== Processing dataset: {dataset_name} ===\")\n        # Load one dataset at a time to save memory\n        if dataset_name == \"sst2\":\n            texts, labels = load_sst2()\n        else:\n            texts, labels = load_imdb()\n\n        # Generate configs for this dataset\n        configs = []\n        for sample_size in SAMPLE_SIZES:\n            for sample_size, imbalance_ratio, seed\n                    ))\n\n        logger.info(f\"Running {len(configs)} configurations for {dataset_name}\")\n\n        # Run in parallel with ProcessPoolExecutor\n        mp_context = mp.get_context(\"spawn\")\n        with ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=NUM_WORKERS, mp_context=mp_context) as executor:\n            futures = {\n                executor.submit(run_single_experiment_with_timeout, *config): config\n                for config in configs\n            }\n\n            for future in as_completed(futures):\n                config = futures[future]\n                try:\n                    result = future.result(timeout=EXPERIMENT_TIMEOUT)\n                    all_results.append(result)\n                except Exception as e:\n                    logger.error(f\"Experiment failed for config {config}: {e}\")\n                    dataset_name_c, _, _, sample_size_c, imbalance_ratio_c, seed_c = config\n                    all_results.append({\n                        'dataset': dataset_name_c,\n                        'sample_size': sample_size_c,\n                        'imbalance_ratio': imbalance_ratio_c,\n                        'seed': seed_c,\n                        'error': str(e),\n                    })\n\n        # Free memory before next dataset\n        del texts, labels, configs\n        gc.collect()\n        logger.info(f\"Finished {dataset_name}, freeing memory\")\n\n    logger.info(f\"Completed {len(all_results)} experiments total\")\n    return all_results\n\n\n# f\"{dataset}_size{sample_size}_imb{imbalance_ratio}\"\n                summary[key] = {\n                    'dataset': dataset,\n                    'sample_size': sample_size,\n with key metrics\n            output_str = (\n                f\"Simple accuracy: {r['simple_accuracy']:.3f}, \"\n                f\"Complex accuracy: {r['complex_accuracy']:.3f}, \"\n                f\"Disagreements: {r['num_disagreements']}/{r['test_size']} \"\n                f\"({r['disagreement_ratio']:.1%}), \"\n                f\"Directional rule accuracy: {r['directional_rule_accuracy']:.3f}\"\n            )\n\n            example = {\n                'input': input_str,\n                'output': output_str,\n                'metadata_dataset':  'metadata_train_size': r['train_size'],\n                'metadata_test_size': r['test_size'],\n                'metadata_majority_class': r['majority_class'],\n                'metadata_disagreement_ratio': r['disagreement_ratio'],\n                'metadata_num_disagreements': r['num_disagreements'],\n                'predict_simple_model': f\"accuracy={r['simple_accuracy']:.3f}\",\n                'predict_complex_model': f\"accuracy={r['complex_accuracy']:.3f}\",\n                'predict_directional_rule': f\"accuracy={r['directional_rule_accuracy']:.3f},p={r['directional_rule_pvalue']:.3f}\",\n                'predict_confidence_baseline': f\"accuracy={r['confidence_baseline_accuracy']:.3f}\",\n                'predict_trust_score_baseline': f\"accuracy={r['trust_score_baseline_accuracy']:.3f}\",\n                'predict_random_baseline': f\"accuracy={r['random_baseline_accuracy']:.3f}\"\n            }\n\n            examples.append(example)\n\n        datasets_output.append({\n            'dataset': dataset_name,\n            'examples': examples\n        })\n\n    # Main output in exp_gen_sol_out format\n    output = {\n        'metadata': {\n            'description': 'Disagreement Direction Test for Sentiment Classification',\n            'sample_sizes': SAMPLE_SIZES,\n            'imbalance_ratios': IMBALANCE_RATIOS,\n            'seeds': SEEDS,\n            'total_configurations': len(results),\n            'ablation_table': ablation\n        },\n        'datasets': datasets_output\n    }\n\n    output_path = OUTPUT_DIR / \"method_out.json\"\n    output_path.write_text(json.dumps(output, indent=2, default=str))\n    logger.info(f\"Saved results to {output_path}\")\n\n    # Also save as method_out.json in workspace root for validation\n    workspace_output = WORKSPACE / \"method_out.json\"\n    workspace_output.write_text(json.dumps(output, ============================================================================\n\ndef validate_results(results: list[dict]) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Validate that all required fields are present in 'confidence_baseline_accuracy', 'trust_score_baseline_accuracy',\n        'random_baseline_accuracy'\n    ]\n\n    valid = True\n    for i, result in enumerate(results):\n        if 'error' in logger.error(f\"Result {i} missing field: {field}\")\n                valid = False\n\n        # Check disagreement counts\n        if result.get('num_disagreements', 0) > 0:\n            # Additional validation could go here\n            pass\n\n    if valid:\n        logger.info(\"All results validated successfully\")\n    else:\n        logger.error(\"Validation failed\")\n\n    return valid\n\n\ndef smoke_test():\n    \"\"\"Run smoke test with one dataset, one seed, size=100.\"\"\"\n    logger.info(\"Running smoke test\")\n\n    try:\n        result = run_single_experiment(\n            dataset_name='sst2',\n            texts=['sample text 1', 'sample text 2'] * 50,  # Dummy data for quick test\n            labels=[0, 1] * 50,\n            sample_size=100,\n            imbalance_ratio=0.5,\n            seed=0\n        )\n\n        assert 'num_disagreements' in result\n        assert 'directional_rule_accuracy' in result\n        assert 'confidence_baseline_accuracy' in result\n\n        logger.info(\"Smoke test passed\")\n        return True\n\n    except Exception as e:\n        logger.error(f\"Smoke test failed: {e}\")\n        return False\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# MAIN\n# ============================================================================\n\n@logger.catch(reraise=True)\ndef main():\n    logger.info(\"Starting Disagreement Direction Test for Sentiment\")\n\n    # Run smoke test first\n    # smoke_test()  # Skip for now, will use real data\n\n    # Run all experiments\n    results = run_all_experiments()\n\n    # Validate results\n    validate_results(results)\n\n    # Generate ablation table\n    ablation = generate_ablation_table(results)\n\n    # Save results\n    save_results(results, ablation)\n\n    # Print summary\n    print(\"\\n\" + \"=\"*60)\n    print(\"EXPERIMENT SUMMARY\")\n    print(\"=\"*60)\n\n    # Overall statistics\n    valid_results = [r for r in results if 'error' not in r]\n    total_disagreements = sum(r['num_disagreements'] for r in valid_results)\n    mean_dir_acc = np.mean([r['directional_rule_accuracy'] for r in valid_results])\n    mean_conf_acc = np.mean([r['confidence_baseline_accuracy'] for r in valid_results])\n    mean_trust_acc = np.mean([r['trust_score_baseline_accuracy'] for r in valid_results])\n    mean_rand_acc = np.mean([r['random_baseline_accuracy'] for r in valid_results])\n\n    print(f\"Total configurations run: {len(valid_results)}\")\n    print(f\"Total disagreements analyzed: {total_disagreements}\")\n    print(f\"Mean directional rule accuracy: {mean_dir_acc:.3f}\")\n    print(f\"Mean confidence baseline accuracy: {mean_conf_acc:.3f}\")\n    print(f\"Mean trust score baseline accuracy: {mean_trust_acc:.3f}\")\n    print(f\"Mean random baseline accuracy: {mean_rand_acc:.3f}\")\n    print(\"=\"*60 + \"\\n\")\n\n    logger.info(\"Experiment completed successfully\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n", "new_content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Disagreement Direction Test for Sentiment Classification.\n\nCompares TF-IDF Logistic Regression vs character n-gram RandomForest\non small sentiment datasets, analyzing whether disagreement direction\npredicts the correct label better than chance and concrete baselines.\n\nHypothesis: When a simple model and complex model disagree, the simple\nmodel is more likely correct when it predicts the majority class\n(because it biases toward the mode), and the complex model is more\nlikely correct when the simple model predicts the minority class\n(because the simple model is unreliable on rare patterns).\n\"\"\"\n\nimport gc\nimport json\nimport math\nimport multiprocessing as mp\nimport os\nimport resource\nimport sys\nimport time\nfrom collections import Counter\nfrom concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor, as_completed\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Any\n\nimport numpy as np\nfrom datasets import load_dataset\nfrom loguru import logger\nfrom scipy import stats\nfrom scipy.stats import binomtest\nfrom sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier\nfrom sklearn.feature_extraction.text import CountVectorizer, TfidfVectorizer\nfrom sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression\nfrom sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score\nfrom sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split\nfrom sklearn.neighbors import NearestNeighbors\nfrom sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline\n\n# ============================================================================\n# CONFIGURATION AND CONSTANTS\n# ============================================================================\n\nWORKSPACE = Path(\n    \"/ai-inventor/aii_data/runs/run_q27XJGeAT3TE/3_invention_loop/iter_1/gen_art/gen_art_experiment_1\"\n)\nLOG_DIR = WORKSPACE / \"logs\"\nOUTPUT_DIR = WORKSPACE / \"results\"\nLOG_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)\nOUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)\n\nDATASETS = [\"sst2\", \"imdb\"]\nSAMPLE_SIZES = [100, 200, 500, 1000]\nIMBALANCE_RATIOS = [1.0, 1.5, 2.0]  # majority:minority ratio (1.0 = balanced)\nSEEDS = list(range(10))\nNUM_WORKERS = 2  # Container has 2 CPUs\n\n# Memory limits based on container resources (14GB RAM)\nRAM_BUDGET = 12 * 1024**3  # 12GB\n\n# Experiment timeout per configuration (seconds)\nEXPERIMENT_TIMEOUT = 120  # 2 minutes per config\n\n# ============================================================================\n# LOGGING SETUP\n# ============================================================================\n\nlogger.remove()\nlogger.add(\n    sys.stdout,\n    level=\"INFO\",\n    format=\"{time:HH:mm:ss}|{level:<7}|{message}\",\n)\nlogger.add(\n    LOG_DIR / \"run.log\",\n    rotation=\"30 MB\",\n    level=\"DEBUG\",\n)\n\n# ============================================================================\n# HARDWARE DETECTION\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef _detect_cpus() -> int:\n    \"\"\"Detect actual CPU allocation (containers/pods/bare metal).\"\"\"\n    try:  # cgroups v2 quota\n        parts = Path(\"/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.max\").read_text().split()\n        if parts[0] != \"max\":\n            return max(1, math.ceil(int(parts[0]) / int(parts[1])))\n    except (FileNotFoundError, ValueError):\n        pass\n    try:  # cgroups v1 quota\n        q = int(Path(\"/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/cpu.cfs_quota_us\").read_text())\n        p = int(Path(\"/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/cpu.cfs_period_us\").read_text())\n        if q > 0:\n            return max(1, math.ceil(q / p))\n    except (FileNotFoundError, ValueError):\n        pass\n    try:  # CPU affinity (cpuset \u2014 used by RunPod, Docker --cpuset-cpus)\n        return len(os.sched_getaffinity(0))\n    except (AttributeError, OSError):\n        pass\n    return os.cpu_count() or 1\n\nNUM_CPUS = _detect_cpus()\nlogger.info(f\"Detected {NUM_CPUS} CPUs\")\n\n# Set memory limits\nresource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_AS, (RAM_BUDGET * 3, RAM_BUDGET * 3))\n\n# ============================================================================\n# MODEL DEFINITIONS\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef get_simple_model():\n    \"\"\"Simple model: TF-IDF + Logistic Regression.\"\"\"\n    return Pipeline([\n        ('tfidf', TfidfVectorizer(max_features=10000, ngram_range=(1, 2))),\n        ('clf', LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000, random_state=42, n_jobs=1))\n    ])\n\n\ndef get_complex_model():\n    \"\"\"Complex model: character n-grams + RandomForest.\"\"\"\n    return Pipeline([\n        ('char_ngram', CountVectorizer(\n            analyzer='char',\n            ngram_range=(3, 5),\n            max_features=20000\n        )),\n        ('clf', RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=100, random_state=42, n_jobs=1))\n    ])\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# DATA LOADING AND PREPARATION\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef load_sst2():\n    \"\"\"Load SST-2 dataset.\"\"\"\n    logger.info(\"Loading SST-2 dataset\")\n    ds = load_dataset(\"stanfordnlp/sst2\", split=\"train\")\n    texts = ds[\"sentence\"]\n    labels = ds[\"label\"]\n    del ds\n    gc.collect()\n    return texts, labels\n\n\ndef load_imdb():\n    \"\"\"Load IMDB dataset.\"\"\"\n    logger.info(\"Loading IMDB dataset\")\n    ds = load_dataset(\"stanfordnlp/imdb\", split=\"train\")\n    texts = ds[\"text\"]\n    labels = ds[\"label\"]\n    del ds\n    gc.collect()\n    return texts, labels\n\n\ndef stratified_imbalanced_subsample(\n    texts: list[str],\n    labels: list[int],\n    target_size: int,\n    imbalance_ratio: float,\n    random_state: int\n) -> tuple[list[str], list[int]]:\n    \"\"\"Create a stratified subsample with controlled class imbalance.\n\n    Args:\n        texts: List of text samples\n        labels: List of labels\n        target_size: Total target sample size\n        imbalance_ratio: Ratio of majority to minority class (1.0 = balanced)\n        random_state: Random seed\n\n    Returns:\n        Subsampled texts and labels\n    \"\"\"\n    rng = np.random.RandomState(random_state)\n\n    # Separate by class\n    class_0_idx = [i for i, l in enumerate(labels) if l == 0]\n    class_1_idx = [i for i, l in enumerate(labels) if l == 1]\n\n    # Calculate sizes based on imbalance ratio\n    # imbalance_ratio = majority_size / minority_size\n    # total = majority_size + minority_size\n    minority_size = int(target_size / (1 + imbalance_ratio))\n    majority_size = target_size - minority_size\n\n    # Determine which class has more available samples\n    if len(class_0_idx) >= len(class_1_idx):\n        majority_class_idx = class_0_idx\n        minority_class_idx = class_1_idx\n    else:\n        majority_class_idx = class_1_idx\n        minority_class_idx = class_0_idx\n\n    # Sample from each class\n    sampled_majority = rng.choice(\n        majority_class_idx,\n        size=min(majority_size, len(majority_class_idx)),\n        replace=False\n    )\n    sampled_minority = rng.choice(\n        minority_class_idx,\n        size=min(minority_size, len(minority_class_idx)),\n        replace=False\n    )\n\n    # Combine and shuffle\n    indices = np.concatenate([sampled_majority, sampled_minority])\n    rng.shuffle(indices)\n\n    return [texts[i] for i in indices], [labels[i] for i in indices]\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# BASELINE METHODS\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef confidence_baseline(disagreements: list[dict]) -> list[int]:\n    \"\"\"Baseline: predict whichever model has higher confidence.\"\"\"\n    predictions = []\n    for d in disagreements:\n        if d['prob_simple'] > d['prob_complex']:\n            predictions.append(d['pred_simple'])\n        else:\n            predictions.append(d['pred_complex'])\n    return predictions\n\n\ndef trust_score_baseline(\n    disagreements: list[dict],\n    train_texts: list[str],\n    train_labels: list[int]\n) -> list[int]:\n    \"\"\"Baseline: trust-score style proxy using nearest-neighbor agreement in TF-IDF space.\"\"\"\n    vectorizer = TfidfVectorizer(max_features=10000, ngram_range=(1, 2))\n    try:\n        train_tfidf = vectorizer.fit_transform(train_texts)\n        nn = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=5, metric='cosine')\n        nn.fit(train_tfidf)\n\n        predictions = []\n        for d in disagreements:\n            test_vec = vectorizer.transform([d['text']])\n            _, indices = nn.kneighbors(test_vec)\n            neighbor_labels = [train_labels[i] for i in indices[0]]\n            majority_label = Counter(neighbor_labels).most_common(1)[0][0]\n            predictions.append(majority_label)\n    except Exception as e:\n        logger.warning(f\"Trust score baseline failed: {e}\")\n        # Fallback to random\n        rng = np.random.RandomState(42)\n        predictions = rng.randint(0, 2, size=len(disagreements)).tolist()\n\n    return predictions\n\n\ndef random_baseline(n: int) -> list[int]:\n    \"\"\"Random baseline.\"\"\"\n    return np.random.RandomState(42).randint(0, 2, size=n).tolist()\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# STATISTICAL TESTS\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef binomial_test_on_directional_rule(\n    disagreements: list[dict],\n    majority_class: int\n) -> tuple[float, float]:\n    \"\"\"Test if directional rule accuracy > 50% using binomial test.\"\"\"\n    correct = sum(\n        1 for d in disagreements\n        if (d['pred_simple'] == majority_class and d['pred_simple'] == d['true_label']) or\n           (d['pred_simple'] != majority_class and d['pred_complex'] == d['true_label'])\n    )\n    n = len(disagreements)\n    if n == 0:\n        return 0.0, 1.0\n    result = binomtest(correct, n, 0.5, alternative='greater')\n    p_value = result.pvalue\n    accuracy = correct / n\n    return accuracy, p_value\n\n\ndef mcnemar_test(\n    y_true: list[int],\n    pred1: list[int],\n    pred2: list[int]\n) -> tuple[float, float]:\n    \"\"\"McNemar's test between two prediction sets.\"\"\"\n    a = sum(1 for yt, p1, p2 in zip(y_true, pred1, pred2)\n            if p1 == yt and p2 != yt)  # pred1 correct, pred2 wrong\n    b = sum(1 for yt, p1, p2 in zip(y_true, pred1, pred2)\n            if p1 != yt and p2 == yt)  # pred1 wrong, pred2 correct\n    d = sum(1 for yt, p1, p2 in zip(y_true, pred1, pred2)\n            if p1 == yt and p2 == yt)  # both correct\n\n    if a + b == 0:\n        return 0.0, 1.0\n\n    if a + b < 25:\n        result = binomtest(a, a + b, 0.5, alternative='two-sided')\n        p_value = result.pvalue\n    else:\n        chi2 = (abs(a - b) - 1) ** 2 / (a + b)\n        p_value = stats.chi2.sf(chi2, 1)\n\n    accuracy1 = (a + d) / len(y_true) if len(y_true) > 0 else 0\n    accuracy2 = (b + d) / len(y_true) if len(y_true) > 0 else 0\n\n    return accuracy1, p_value\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# EXPERIMENT EXECUTION\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef run_single_experiment(\n    dataset_name: str,\n    texts: list[str],\n    labels: list[int],\n    sample_size: int,\n    imbalance_ratio: float,\n    seed: int\n) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"Run a single experiment configuration.\"\"\"\n    start_time = time.time()\n    logger.info(\n        f\"Running: dataset={dataset_name}, size={sample_size}, \"\n        f\"imbalance={imbalance_ratio},  return float('nan')\n    return float(np.mean(clean))\n\n\ndef _safe_std(values: list[float]) -> float:\n    \"\"\"Compute std ignoring NaN values; return NaN if fewer than 2 valid.\"\"\"\n    clean = {\n                    'dataset': dataset,\n                    'sample_size': sample_size,\n                    'imbalance_ratio': imbalance_ratio,\n                    'n_seeds':  f\"Simple accuracy: {r['simple_accuracy']:.3f}, \"\n                f\"Complex accuracy: {r['complex_accuracy']:.3f}, \"\n                f\"Disagreements: {r['num_disagreements']}/{r['test_size']} "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Disagreement Direction Test for Sentiment Classification.\n\nCompares TF-IDF Logistic Regression vs character n-gram RandomForest\non small sentiment datasets, analyzing whether disagreement direction\npredicts the correct label better than chance and concrete baselines.\n\nHypothesis: When a simple model and complex model disagree, the simple\nmodel is more likely correct when it predicts the majority class\n(because it biases toward the mode), and the complex model is more\nlikely correct when the simple model predicts the minority class\n(because the simple model is unreliable on rare patterns).\n\"\"\"\n\nimport gc\nimport json\nimport math\nimport multiprocessing as mp\nimport os\nimport resource\nimport sys\nimport time\nfrom collections import Counter\nfrom concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor, as_completed\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Any\n\nimport numpy as np\nfrom datasets import load_dataset\nfrom loguru import logger\nfrom scipy import stats\nfrom scipy.stats import binomtest\nfrom sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier\nfrom sklearn.feature_extraction.text import CountVectorizer, TfidfVectorizer\nfrom sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression\nfrom sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score\nfrom sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split\nfrom sklearn.neighbors import NearestNeighbors\nfrom sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline\n\n# ============================================================================\n# CONFIGURATION AND CONSTANTS\n# ============================================================================\n\nWORKSPACE = Path(\n    \"/ai-inventor/aii_data/runs/run_q27XJGeAT3TE/3_invention_loop/iter_1/gen_art/gen_art_experiment_1\"\n)\nLOG_DIR = WORKSPACE / \"logs\"\nOUTPUT_DIR = WORKSPACE / \"results\"\nLOG_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)\nOUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)\n\nDATASETS = [\"sst2\", \"imdb\"]\nSAMPLE_SIZES = [100, 200, 500, 1000]\nIMBALANCE_RATIOS = [1.0, 1.5, 2.0]  # majority:minority ratio (1.0 = balanced)\nSEEDS = list(range(10))\nNUM_WORKERS = 2  # Container has 2 CPUs\n\n# Memory limits based on container resources (14GB RAM)\nRAM_BUDGET = 12 * 1024**3  # 12GB\n\n# Experiment timeout per configuration (seconds)\nEXPERIMENT_TIMEOUT = 120  # 2 minutes per config\n\n# ============================================================================\n# LOGGING SETUP\n# ============================================================================\n\nlogger.remove()\nlogger.add(\n    sys.stdout,\n    level=\"INFO\",\n    format=\"{time:HH:mm:ss}|{level:<7}|{message}\",\n)\nlogger.add(\n    LOG_DIR / \"run.log\",\n    rotation=\"30 MB\",\n    level=\"DEBUG\",\n)\n\n# ============================================================================\n# HARDWARE DETECTION\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef _detect_cpus() -> int:\n    \"\"\"Detect actual CPU allocation (containers/pods/bare metal).\"\"\"\n    try:  # cgroups v2 quota\n        parts = Path(\"/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.max\").read_text().split()\n        if parts[0] != \"max\":\n            return max(1, math.ceil(int(parts[0]) / int(parts[1])))\n    except (FileNotFoundError, ValueError):\n        pass\n    try:  # cgroups v1 quota\n        q = int(Path(\"/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/cpu.cfs_quota_us\").read_text())\n        p = int(Path(\"/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/cpu.cfs_period_us\").read_text())\n        if q > 0:\n            return max(1, math.ceil(q / p))\n    except (FileNotFoundError, ValueError):\n        pass\n    try:  # CPU affinity (cpuset \u2014 used by RunPod, Docker --cpuset-cpus)\n        return len(os.sched_getaffinity(0))\n    except (AttributeError, OSError):\n        pass\n    return os.cpu_count() or 1\n\nNUM_CPUS = _detect_cpus()\nlogger.info(f\"Detected {NUM_CPUS} CPUs\")\n\n# Set memory limits\nresource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_AS, (RAM_BUDGET * 3, RAM_BUDGET * 3))\n\n# ============================================================================\n# MODEL DEFINITIONS\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef get_simple_model():\n    \"\"\"Simple model: TF-IDF + Logistic Regression.\"\"\"\n    return Pipeline([\n        ('tfidf', TfidfVectorizer(max_features=10000, ngram_range=(1, 2))),\n        ('clf', LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000, random_state=42, n_jobs=1))\n    ])\n\n\ndef get_complex_model():\n    \"\"\"Complex model: character n-grams + RandomForest.\"\"\"\n    return Pipeline([\n        ('char_ngram', CountVectorizer(\n            analyzer='char',\n            ngram_range=(3, 5),\n            max_features=20000\n        )),\n        ('clf', RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=100, random_state=42, n_jobs=1))\n    ])\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# DATA LOADING AND PREPARATION\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef load_sst2():\n    \"\"\"Load SST-2 dataset.\"\"\"\n    logger.info(\"Loading SST-2 dataset\")\n    ds = load_dataset(\"stanfordnlp/sst2\", split=\"train\")\n    texts = ds[\"sentence\"]\n    labels = ds[\"label\"]\n    del ds\n    gc.collect()\n    return texts, labels\n\n\ndef load_imdb():\n    \"\"\"Load IMDB dataset.\"\"\"\n    logger.info(\"Loading IMDB dataset\")\n    ds = load_dataset(\"stanfordnlp/imdb\", split=\"train\")\n    texts = ds[\"text\"]\n    labels = ds[\"label\"]\n    del ds\n    gc.collect()\n    return texts, labels\n\n\ndef stratified_imbalanced_subsample(\n    texts: list[str],\n    labels: list[int],\n    target_size: int,\n    imbalance_ratio: float,\n    random_state: int\n) -> tuple[list[str], list[int]]:\n    \"\"\"Create a stratified subsample with controlled class imbalance.\n\n    Args:\n        texts: List of text samples\n        labels: List of labels\n        target_size: Total target sample size\n        imbalance_ratio: Ratio of majority to minority class (1.0 = balanced)\n        random_state: Random seed\n\n    Returns:\n        Subsampled texts and labels\n    \"\"\"\n    rng = np.random.RandomState(random_state)\n\n    # Separate by class\n    class_0_idx = [i for i, l in enumerate(labels) if l == 0]\n    class_1_idx = [i for i, l in enumerate(labels) if l == 1]\n\n    # Calculate sizes based on imbalance ratio\n    # imbalance_ratio = majority_size / minority_size\n    # total = majority_size + minority_size\n    minority_size = int(target_size / (1 + imbalance_ratio))\n    majority_size = target_size - minority_size\n\n    # Determine which class has more available samples\n    if len(class_0_idx) >= len(class_1_idx):\n        majority_class_idx = class_0_idx\n        minority_class_idx = class_1_idx\n    else:\n        majority_class_idx = class_1_idx\n        minority_class_idx = class_0_idx\n\n    # Sample from each class\n    sampled_majority = rng.choice(\n        majority_class_idx,\n        size=min(majority_size, len(majority_class_idx)),\n        replace=False\n    )\n    sampled_minority = rng.choice(\n        minority_class_idx,\n        size=min(minority_size, len(minority_class_idx)),\n        replace=False\n    )\n\n    # Combine and shuffle\n    indices = np.concatenate([sampled_majority, sampled_minority])\n    rng.shuffle(indices)\n\n    return [texts[i] for i in indices], [labels[i] for i in indices]\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# BASELINE METHODS\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef confidence_baseline(disagreements: list[dict]) -> list[int]:\n    \"\"\"Baseline: predict whichever model has higher confidence.\"\"\"\n    predictions = []\n    for d in disagreements:\n        if d['prob_simple'] > d['prob_complex']:\n            predictions.append(d['pred_simple'])\n        else:\n            predictions.append(d['pred_complex'])\n    return predictions\n\n\ndef trust_score_baseline(\n    disagreements: list[dict],\n    train_texts: list[str],\n    train_labels: list[int]\n) -> list[int]:\n    \"\"\"Baseline: trust-score style proxy using nearest-neighbor agreement in TF-IDF space.\"\"\"\n    vectorizer = TfidfVectorizer(max_features=10000, ngram_range=(1, 2))\n    try:\n        train_tfidf = vectorizer.fit_transform(train_texts)\n        nn = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=5, metric='cosine')\n        nn.fit(train_tfidf)\n\n        predictions = []\n        for d in disagreements:\n            test_vec = vectorizer.transform([d['text']])\n            _, indices = nn.kneighbors(test_vec)\n            neighbor_labels = [train_labels[i] for i in indices[0]]\n            majority_label = Counter(neighbor_labels).most_common(1)[0][0]\n            predictions.append(majority_label)\n    except Exception as e:\n        logger.warning(f\"Trust score baseline failed: {e}\")\n        # Fallback to random\n        rng = np.random.RandomState(42)\n        predictions = rng.randint(0, 2, size=len(disagreements)).tolist()\n\n    return predictions\n\n\ndef random_baseline(n: int) -> list[int]:\n    \"\"\"Random baseline.\"\"\"\n    return np.random.RandomState(42).randint(0, 2, size=n).tolist()\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# STATISTICAL TESTS\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef binomial_test_on_directional_rule(\n    disagreements: list[dict],\n    majority_class: int\n) -> tuple[float, float]:\n    \"\"\"Test if directional rule accuracy > 50% using binomial test.\"\"\"\n    correct = sum(\n        1 for d in disagreements\n        if (d['pred_simple'] == majority_class and d['pred_simple'] == d['true_label']) or\n           (d['pred_simple'] != majority_class and d['pred_complex'] == d['true_label'])\n    )\n    n = len(disagreements)\n    if n == 0:\n        return 0.0, 1.0\n    result = binomtest(correct, n, 0.5, alternative='greater')\n    p_value = result.pvalue\n    accuracy = correct / n\n    return accuracy, p_value\n\n\ndef mcnemar_test(\n    y_true: list[int],\n    pred1: list[int],\n    pred2: list[int]\n) -> tuple[float, float]:\n    \"\"\"McNemar's test between two prediction sets.\"\"\"\n    a = sum(1 for yt, p1, p2 in zip(y_true, pred1, pred2)\n            if p1 == yt and p2 != yt)  # pred1 correct, pred2 wrong\n    b = sum(1 for yt, p1, p2 in zip(y_true, pred1, pred2)\n            if p1 != yt and p2 == yt)  # pred1 wrong, pred2 correct\n    d = sum(1 for yt, p1, p2 in zip(y_true, pred1, pred2)\n            if p1 == yt and p2 == yt)  # both correct\n\n    if a + b == 0:\n        return 0.0, 1.0\n\n    if a + b < 25:\n        result = binomtest(a, a + b, 0.5, alternative='two-sided')\n        p_value = result.pvalue\n    else:\n        chi2 = (abs(a - b) - 1) ** 2 / (a + b)\n        p_value = stats.chi2.sf(chi2, 1)\n\n    accuracy1 = (a + d) / len(y_true) if len(y_true) > 0 else 0\n    accuracy2 = (b + d) / len(y_true) if len(y_true) > 0 else 0\n\n    return accuracy1, p_value\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# EXPERIMENT EXECUTION\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef run_single_experiment(\n    dataset_name: str,\n    texts: list[str],\n    labels: list[int],\n    sample_size: int,\n    imbalance_ratio: float,\n    seed: int\n) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"Run a single experiment configuration.\"\"\"\n    start_time = time.time()\n    logger.info(\n        f\"Running: dataset={dataset_name}, size={sample_size}, \"\n        f\"imbalance={imbalance_ratio}, seed={seed}\"\n    )\n\n    # Subsample\n    sub_texts, sub_labels = stratified_imbalanced_subsample(\n        texts, labels, sample_size, imbalance_ratio, seed\n    )\n\n    # Determine majority class\n    label_counts = Counter(sub_labels)\n    majority_class = label_counts.most_common(1)[0][0]\n    logger.debug(f\"Majority class: {majority_class}, distribution: {label_counts}\")\n\n    # "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Disagreement Direction Test for Sentiment Classification.\n\nCompares TF-IDF Logistic Regression vs character n-gram RandomForest\non small sentiment datasets, analyzing whether disagreement direction\npredicts the correct label better than chance and concrete baselines.\n\nHypothesis: When a simple model and complex model disagree, the simple\nmodel is more likely correct when it predicts the majority class\n(because it biases toward the mode), and the complex model is more\nlikely correct when the simple model predicts the minority class\n(because the simple model is unreliable on rare patterns).\n\"\"\"\n\nimport gc\nimport json\nimport math\nimport multiprocessing as mp\nimport os\nimport resource\nimport sys\nimport time\nfrom collections import Counter\nfrom concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor, as_completed\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Any\n\nimport numpy as np\nfrom datasets import load_dataset\nfrom loguru import logger\nfrom scipy import stats\nfrom scipy.stats import binomtest\nfrom sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier\nfrom sklearn.feature_extraction.text import CountVectorizer, TfidfVectorizer\nfrom sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression\nfrom sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score\nfrom sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split\nfrom sklearn.neighbors import NearestNeighbors\nfrom sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline\n\n# ============================================================================\n# CONFIGURATION AND CONSTANTS\n# ============================================================================\n\nWORKSPACE = Path(\n    \"/ai-inventor/aii_data/runs/run_q27XJGeAT3TE/3_invention_loop/iter_1/gen_art/gen_art_experiment_1\"\n)\nLOG_DIR = WORKSPACE / \"logs\"\nOUTPUT_DIR = WORKSPACE / \"results\"\nLOG_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)\nOUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)\n\nDATASETS = [\"sst2\", \"imdb\"]\nSAMPLE_SIZES = [100, 200, 500, 1000]\nIMBALANCE_RATIOS = [1.0, 1.5, 2.0]  # majority:minority ratio (1.0 = balanced)\nSEEDS = list(range(10))\nNUM_WORKERS = 2  # Container has 2 CPUs\n\n# Memory limits based on container resources (14GB RAM)\nRAM_BUDGET = 12 * 1024**3  # 12GB\n\n# Experiment timeout per configuration (seconds)\nEXPERIMENT_TIMEOUT = 120  # 2 minutes per config\n\n# ============================================================================\n# LOGGING SETUP\n# ============================================================================\n\nlogger.remove()\nlogger.add(\n    sys.stdout,\n    level=\"INFO\",\n    format=\"{time:HH:mm:ss}|{level:<7}|{message}\",\n)\nlogger.add(\n    LOG_DIR / \"run.log\",\n    rotation=\"30 MB\",\n    level=\"DEBUG\",\n)\n\n# ============================================================================\n# HARDWARE DETECTION\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef _detect_cpus() -> int:\n    \"\"\"Detect actual CPU allocation (containers/pods/bare metal).\"\"\"\n    try:  # cgroups v2 quota\n        parts = Path(\"/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.max\").read_text().split()\n        if parts[0] != \"max\":\n            return max(1, math.ceil(int(parts[0]) / int(parts[1])))\n    except (FileNotFoundError, ValueError):\n        pass\n    try:  # cgroups v1 quota\n        q = int(Path(\"/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/cpu.cfs_quota_us\").read_text())\n        p = int(Path(\"/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/cpu.cfs_period_us\").read_text())\n        if q > 0:\n            return max(1, math.ceil(q / p))\n    except (FileNotFoundError, ValueError):\n        pass\n    try:  # CPU affinity (cpuset \u2014 used by RunPod, Docker --cpuset-cpus)\n        return len(os.sched_getaffinity(0))\n    except (AttributeError, OSError):\n        pass\n    return os.cpu_count() or 1\n\nNUM_CPUS = _detect_cpus()\nlogger.info(f\"Detected {NUM_CPUS} CPUs\")\n\n# Set memory limits\nresource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_AS, (RAM_BUDGET * 3, RAM_BUDGET * 3))\n\n# ============================================================================\n# MODEL DEFINITIONS\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef get_simple_model():\n    \"\"\"Simple model: TF-IDF + Logistic Regression.\"\"\"\n    return Pipeline([\n        ('tfidf', TfidfVectorizer(max_features=10000, ngram_range=(1, 2))),\n        ('clf', LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000, random_state=42, n_jobs=1))\n    ])\n\n\ndef get_complex_model():\n    \"\"\"Complex model: character n-grams + RandomForest.\"\"\"\n    return Pipeline([\n        ('char_ngram', CountVectorizer(\n            analyzer='char',\n            ngram_range=(3, 5),\n            max_features=20000\n        )),\n        ('clf', RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=100, random_state=42, n_jobs=1))\n    ])\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# DATA LOADING AND PREPARATION\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef load_sst2():\n    \"\"\"Load SST-2 dataset.\"\"\"\n    logger.info(\"Loading SST-2 dataset\")\n    ds = load_dataset(\"stanfordnlp/sst2\", split=\"train\")\n    texts = ds[\"sentence\"]\n    labels = ds[\"label\"]\n    del ds\n    gc.collect()\n    return texts, labels\n\n\ndef load_imdb():\n    \"\"\"Load IMDB dataset.\"\"\"\n    logger.info(\"Loading IMDB dataset\")\n    ds = load_dataset(\"stanfordnlp/imdb\", split=\"train\")\n    texts = ds[\"text\"]\n    labels = ds[\"label\"]\n    del ds\n    gc.collect()\n    return texts, labels\n\n\ndef stratified_imbalanced_subsample(\n    texts: list[str],\n    labels: list[int],\n    target_size: int,\n    imbalance_ratio: float,\n    random_state: int\n) -> tuple[list[str], list[int]]:\n    \"\"\"Create a stratified subsample with controlled class imbalance.\n\n    Args:\n        texts: List of text samples\n        labels: List of labels\n        target_size: Total target sample size\n        imbalance_ratio: Ratio of majority to minority class (1.0 = balanced)\n        random_state: Random seed\n\n    Returns:\n        Subsampled texts and labels\n    \"\"\"\n    rng = np.random.RandomState(random_state)\n\n    # Separate by class\n    class_0_idx = [i for i, l in enumerate(labels) if l == 0]\n    class_1_idx = [i for i, l in enumerate(labels) if l == 1]\n\n    # Calculate sizes based on imbalance ratio\n    # imbalance_ratio = majority_size / minority_size\n    # total = majority_size + minority_size\n    minority_size = int(target_size / (1 + imbalance_ratio))\n    majority_size = target_size - minority_size\n\n    # Determine which class has more available samples\n    if len(class_0_idx) >= len(class_1_idx):\n        majority_class_idx = class_0_idx\n        minority_class_idx = class_1_idx\n    else:\n        majority_class_idx = class_1_idx\n        minority_class_idx = class_0_idx\n\n    # Sample from each class\n    sampled_majority = rng.choice(\n        majority_class_idx,\n        size=min(majority_size, len(majority_class_idx)),\n        replace=False\n    )\n    sampled_minority = rng.choice(\n        minority_class_idx,\n        size=min(minority_size, len(minority_class_idx)),\n        replace=False\n    )\n\n    # Combine and shuffle\n    indices = np.concatenate([sampled_majority, sampled_minority])\n    rng.shuffle(indices)\n\n    return [texts[i] for i in indices], [labels[i] for i in indices]\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# BASELINE METHODS\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef confidence_baseline(disagreements: list[dict]) -> list[int]:\n    \"\"\"Baseline: predict whichever model has higher confidence.\"\"\"\n    predictions = []\n    for d in disagreements:\n        if d['prob_simple'] > d['prob_complex']:\n            predictions.append(d['pred_simple'])\n        else:\n            predictions.append(d['pred_complex'])\n    return predictions\n\n\ndef trust_score_baseline(\n    disagreements: list[dict],\n    train_texts: list[str],\n    train_labels: list[int]\n) -> list[int]:\n    \"\"\"Baseline: trust-score style proxy using nearest-neighbor agreement in TF-IDF space.\"\"\"\n    vectorizer = TfidfVectorizer(max_features=10000, ngram_range=(1, 2))\n    try:\n        train_tfidf = vectorizer.fit_transform(train_texts)\n        nn = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=5, metric='cosine')\n        nn.fit(train_tfidf)\n\n        predictions = []\n        for d in disagreements:\n            test_vec = vectorizer.transform([d['text']])\n            _, indices = nn.kneighbors(test_vec)\n            neighbor_labels = [train_labels[i] for i in indices[0]]\n            majority_label = Counter(neighbor_labels).most_common(1)[0][0]\n            predictions.append(majority_label)\n    except Exception as e:\n        logger.warning(f\"Trust score baseline failed: {e}\")\n        # Fallback to random\n        rng = np.random.RandomState(42)\n        predictions = rng.randint(0, 2, size=len(disagreements)).tolist()\n\n    return predictions\n\n\ndef random_baseline(n: int) -> list[int]:\n    \"\"\"Random baseline.\"\"\"\n    return np.random.RandomState(42).randint(0, 2, size=n).tolist()\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# STATISTICAL TESTS\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef binomial_test_on_directional_rule(\n    disagreements: list[dict],\n    majority_class: int\n) -> tuple[float, float]:\n    \"\"\"Test if directional rule accuracy > 50% using binomial test.\"\"\"\n    correct = sum(\n        1 for d in disagreements\n        if (d['pred_simple'] == majority_class and d['pred_simple'] == d['true_label']) or\n           (d['pred_simple'] != majority_class and d['pred_complex'] == d['true_label'])\n    )\n    n = len(disagreements)\n    if n == 0:\n        return 0.0, 1.0\n    result = binomtest(correct, n, 0.5, alternative='greater')\n    p_value = result.pvalue\n    accuracy = correct / n\n    return accuracy, p_value\n\n\ndef mcnemar_test(\n    y_true: list[int],\n    pred1: list[int],\n    pred2: list[int]\n) -> tuple[float, float]:\n    \"\"\"McNemar's test between two prediction sets.\"\"\"\n    a = sum(1 for yt, p1, p2 in zip(y_true, pred1, \"\"\"Create a stratified subsample with controlled class imbalance.\n\n    Args:\n        texts: List of text samples\n        labels: List of labels\n        target_size: Total target sample size\n      random_accuracy = accuracy_score(true_labels_d, random_preds)\n\n        # Statistical tests\n        _, dir_pvalue = binomial_test_on_directional_rule(disagreements, majority_class)\n\n        #
